<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lm:Lupperbound}
    Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian, then $\left\lVert\mathcal{L}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq 2(\left\lVertH\right\rVert + \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert^{2})$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
\begin{align}
        \left\lVert\mathcal{L}\right\rVert_{\infty} &= \sup_{A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}), \braket{A, A} = 1}\braket{\mathcal{L}(A) , \mathcal{L}(A)} =  \sup_{A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}), \left\lVertA\right\rVert_{2} = 1} \left\lVert\mathcal{L}(A)\right\rVert_{2} \nonumber \\
                                    &\leq \sup_{A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}), \left\lVertA\right\rVert_{2} = 1} \left(\left\lVertHA\right\rVert_{2} + \left\lVertAH\right\rVert_{2} + \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\left\lVertL_{\mu}AL_{\mu}^{*}\right\rVert_{2} + \frac{1}{2}\left\lVertL_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}A\right\rVert_{2} + \frac{1}{2}\left\lVertAL_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\right\rVert_{2}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                    &\leq \left(2\left\lVertH\right\rVert  + \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert^{2} + \left\lVertL_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\right\rVert\right)\right) \leq 2\left(\left\lVertH\right\rVert + \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert^{2}\right)
    \end{align}
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lm:repartL}
    Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian dissipator, then for all $\ket{\psi} , \ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}$, $\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi})} \leq 0$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}$, then
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi})} &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\phi} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi} + \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\phi}) - \frac{1}{2}\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \frac{1}{2}\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\Big(- \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} -2 \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\phi}) + |\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}|^{2} )\nonumber \\
                                                                               &+ \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}) + \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}|^{2}) - \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\Big( |\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} + |\bra{\phi}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}|^{2} - \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi} - |\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}|^{2}\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &\leq \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\Big(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\braket{\psi|\psi} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} + \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi}\braket{\phi|\phi} - \bra{\phi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\phi} \Big) = 0.
    \end{align}
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lm:opmap}
    Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a bounded linear operator on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ defined by $\mathcal{M}(\bullet) = \sum_{\mu}A_{\mu} \bullet B_{\mu}$ for $A_{\mu}, B_{\mu} \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, then $\mathrm{Op}(\mathcal{M}) = \sum_{\mu}A_{\mu}\otimes \bar{B}_{\mu}.$
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:QMA}
    A promise promblem \textsc{L} is in $\mathrm{QMA}$ if there exists a polynomial-time uniform family of quantum circuits $V_{x}$ acting on register $P$ of $\operatorname{poly}(|x|)$ qubits such that for every instance $x$ of problem \textsc{L},
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} if $x \in \textsc{L}_{A}$ then there exists a quantum state $\ket{\psi_{x}} \in \mathcal{H}_{P}$ such that $\mathrm{Pr}\left[\mathrm{accept} \; | \; V_{x}\ket{\psi_{x}}\right] \geq b$.
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} if $x \in \textsc{L}_{R}$ then for all states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{P}$, $\mathrm{Pr}\left[\mathrm{accept} \; | \; V_{x}\ket{\psi}\right] \leq a$.
    \end{itemize}
    where $b - a \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)$  and $0 < \epsilon < a < b < 1 - \epsilon$ with $\epsilon \geq 1 / 2^{-\operatorname{poly}(n)}$. For $b=1$ the class is denoted $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lm:steadystatecond}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a Lindbladian dissipator generated by jump operators $\{L_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m}$, then $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) = 0$ if and only if for all $\mu \in [m]$, $L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = c_{\mu}\ket{\psi}$ and $\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}|c_{\mu}|^{2} \ket{\psi}$
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lm:restrictdfscond}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a Lindbladian dissipator generated by jump operators $\{L_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m}$ where $L_{\mu} = \L_{\mu}^{*}$, then $\mathcal{D}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) = 0$ if and only if for all $\mu \in [m]$, $L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = c_{\mu}\ket{\psi}$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Consider the backwards direction. We have for all $\mu\in [m]$, $L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = c_{\mu}\ket{\psi}$ from our assumption, in-addtion, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \sum_{\gamma=1}^{m}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = \sum_{\gamma=1}^{m}L_{\mu}^{2}\ket{\psi} =  \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}c_{\mu}^{2}\ket{\psi}  = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}|c_{\mu}|^{2}\ket{\psi}.
    \end{equation}
    Thus by Lemma~\ref{lm:steadystatecond} we have $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) = 0$ implying the statement of the backwards direction. Since the forward direction of the statement is implied by Lemma~\ref{lm:steadystatecond}, the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:restrictdfscond} holds.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:llps}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a $k$-local Lindbladian dissipator acting on $n$ qubits with associated Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, given by jump operators $\{L_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m=\operatorname{poly}(n)}$, with each jump operator having bounded operator norm $\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(n)$ decide,
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$ such that $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) = 0$,
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} for all pure  quantum states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$ and all steady-states $\rho_{\operatorname{\mathrm{ss}}} \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$, $D(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \rho_{\operatorname{\mathrm{ss}}}) \geq 1 /\operatorname{poly}(n)$,
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:ll}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ be a $k$-local Lindbladian dissipator acting on $n$ qubits with associated Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, given by jump operators $\{L_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m=\operatorname{poly}(n)}$, with each jump operator having bounded operator norm $\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(n)$ decide,
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$ such that $|\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \leq a$,
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} for all pure states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$, $|\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq b$,
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case, where $b-a \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lm:dtod}
    Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a Lindbladian, for all $S \in  \ker{\mathcal{L}}$ and $A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$,
    \begin{equation}
        D(A, S) \geq \frac{1}{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}\right\rVert_{\infty}}|\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}(A)}|.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $A \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ and $S \in \ker{\mathcal{L}}$, we find
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(A)}| &= \frac{1}{2}|\braket{\mathcal{L}(A), A} + \braket{A, \mathcal{L}(A)}| \leq  |\braket{A, \mathcal{L}(A - S)}| = |\braket{\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}(A), A - S}| \nonumber \\
                               &\leq \left\lVert\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}(A)\right\rVert_{2}\left\lVertA - S\right\rVert_{2} \leq \left\lVert\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}\right\rVert_{\infty}\left\lVertA - S\right\rVert_{2} \leq \left\lVert\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}\right\rVert_{\infty}\left\lVertA - S\right\rVert_{1} = 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}^{\dagger}\right\rVert_{\infty}D(A, S)
    \end{align}
    which implies the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:dtod}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:rlltollps}
    $\textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} \text{ with } a=0 \leq \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State}$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $(J, 0, b)$ be an instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} with $a=0$. Since $(J, 0, b)$ is a valid instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian}, we have that the set $J$ generates a $k$-local Lindbladian dissipator, in-addition  $\left\lVertL\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(n)$, therefore the set $J$ forms a valid instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State}. Transforming $(J, 0, b)$ to $J$ can be done in constant time. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Completeness:}} \\

    Let $(J, 0, b)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} with $a=0$ and $J$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} generated from $(J, 0, b)$ according to the description above. For $J$ to be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} we require there to exist a $\ket{\psi}$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) =0,
    \end{equation}
    where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ is the Lindbladian dissipator generated by the jump operators $J$. Since $(J, 0, b)$ is an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian}, choose $\ket{\psi}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:LLPStoLL1}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Equation~\eqref{eq:LLPStoLL1} implies
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} = 0.
    \end{equation} 
    which gives us
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:LLPStoLL2}
        \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} -\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} \right) = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Note, from Cauchy-Schwartz inequality we have $|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} \leq \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}$ which implies each of the terms in the sum over $\mu$ in equation~\eqref{eq:LLPStoLL2}  are less than or equal to 0. Therefore equation~\eqref{eq:LLPStoLL2} implies for all $\mu \in [m]$
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:LLPStoLL3}
        |\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} -\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}  = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Let $L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = c_{\mu} \ket{\psi} + d_{\mu} \ket{\psi^{\perp}}$, applying equation~\eqref{eq:LLPStoLL3} we find
    \begin{equation}
        |c_{\mu}|^{2} - (|c_{\mu}|^{2} + |d_{\mu}|^{2}) = -|d_{\mu}|^{2} = 0
    \end{equation}
    which implies for all $\mu \in [m]$
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Lmuis0}
        L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} = c_{\mu} \ket{\psi}.
    \end{equation}
    Since $(J, 0, b)$ forms a valid instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian}, $L_{\mu} = L_{\mu}^{*}$, thus we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:restrictdfscond} of Section~\ref{sec:dfs} implying
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) = 0
    \end{equation}
    as required. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Soundness:}} \\

    Let $(J, 0, b)$ be an \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} with $a=0$ and $J$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} generated from $(J, 0, b)$ according to the description above. For $J$ to be a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} we require for all $\ket{\psi}$ and for all steady-states $\rho_{ss}$ 
    \begin{equation}
        D(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \rho_{ss}) \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)
    \end{equation}
    Since $(J, 0, b)$ is a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} we have for all $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq b,
    \end{equation}
    where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ denotes the Lindbladian dissipator generated by jump operators $J$.
    Applying our distance to decay Lemma, Lemma~\ref{lm:dtod}, we find for all $\ket{\psi}$ and for all steady-states $\rho_{ss}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:tracedist}
        D(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \rho_{ss}) \geq  \frac{1}{2\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{\dagger}\rVert_{\infty}} |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \frac{b}{2\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{\dagger}\rVert_{\infty}}.
    \end{equation}

    Bounding $\lVert \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{\dagger} \rVert_{\infty}$ through Lemma~\ref{lm:Lupperbound} we find,
    \begin{equation}
        \lVert \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{\dagger} \rVert_{\infty} \leq  2\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert^{2}.
    \end{equation}
    Since $(J, 0, b)$ is a valid instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian}, we have $m=\operatorname{poly}(n)$ and for all $\mu \in [m]$, $\left\lVertL_{\mu}\right\rVert = \operatorname{poly}(n)$, thus
    \begin{equation}
        \lVert \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{\dagger} \rVert_{\infty} \leq \operatorname{poly}(n).
    \end{equation}
    In-addition, since $b - a \geq 1 /\operatorname{poly}(n)$ and $a=0$, we have 
    \begin{equation}
        b \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n).
    \end{equation}
    Thus equation~\ref{eq:tracedist} becomes 
    \begin{equation}
        D(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \rho_{ss}) \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)
    \end{equation}
    as required.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:SEPH}
    Let $H$ be a $2k$-local Hamiltonian acting on $2n$ qubits partitioned into $n$ qubit registers $A$ and $B$ with $H$ given by $\{H_{i}\}_{i=1}^{r=\operatorname{poly}(n)}$ where $\mathbb{I} \succeq H_{i} \succeq 0$ and  if $H_{i}$ acts non-trivially on $k'$ qubits in register $A$ then it also acts non-trivially on $k'$ qubits in register $B$, decide
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ such that $(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \leq a$,
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} For all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ and $\ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}_{B}$, $(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}) \geq b$
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case, where $b-a \geq 1 /\operatorname{poly}(n)$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:SEPHinQMA}
    For $k \leq \log(n)$, $\textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} \in \mathrm{QMA}$
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:H}
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:LLtoSEPH}
    For $k \leq \log(n)$, $\textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} \leq \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Let $(J, a, b)$ be an instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} where $J=\{L_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}$ the Lindbladian dissipator generated by jump operators $J$. In-addition let  $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator generated by a single jump operator $L_{\mu}$. From Lemma~\ref{lm:opmap}, we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Op}(\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}) = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\mathrm{Op}(\mathrm{Re}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}) = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\frac{1}{2}\left([L_{\mu}^{*}]_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}]^{\intercal}_{B} + [L_{\mu}]_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}^{* \intercal}]_{B} - [L^{*}_{\mu}L_{\mu}]_{A}\otimes \mathbb{I}_{B} - \mathbb{I}_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}]^{\intercal}_{B} \right),
    \end{equation}
    where each register $A$ and $B$ consist of $n$ qubits each. Define the unnormalized 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:unnormH}
        \tilde{H}_{\mu} = -\frac{1}{2}\left([L_{\mu}^{*}]_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}]^{\intercal}_{B} + [L_{\mu}]_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}^{* \intercal}]_{B} - [L^{*}_{\mu}L_{\mu}]_{A}\otimes \mathbb{I}_{B} - \mathbb{I}_{A} \otimes [L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}]^{\intercal}_{B} \right),
    \end{equation}
    and the normalized-shifted version of $\tilde{H}_{\mu}$ as
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:normshiftedH}
        H_{\mu} = \left(\tilde{H}_{\mu}  - \lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu}  )\mathbb{I}\right) /\sup_{\mu \in [m]}\left(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu} \rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right)
    \end{equation}
    where $\lambda_{0}(A) = \inf_{\lambda \in \mathrm{Sp}\left(A\right)} \lambda $. In-addition define the set $F = \{H_{\mu}\}_{\mu=1}^{m}$ and 
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{cases}
            a' = \left(a - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu}) \right) / \sup_{\mu \in [m]}(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|), \\
            b' = \left(b - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu}) \right) / \sup_{\mu \in [m]}(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|). \\
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    Note, since each $L_{\mu}$ acts non-trivially on at most $k$ qubits, each $H_{\mu}$ acts non-trivially on at most $2k$ qubits, thus $H=\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}H_{\mu}$ is $2k$-local. Furthermore, equation~\eqref{eq:unnormH} implies each $H_{\mu}$ acts on non-trivially on the same number of qubits in register $A$ as it does in register $B$. Moreover, equation~\eqref{eq:normshiftedH} implies $0 \preceq H_{\mu} \preceq \mathbb{I}$. Thus $(F, a', b', A, B)$ forms a valid instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian}. For $k \leq \log(n)$ we can compute each $\tilde{H}_{\mu}$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time using standard matrix manipulation algorithms since each $L_{\mu}$ is a $\operatorname{poly}(n) \times \operatorname{poly}(n)$ dimension matrix. In-addition since each $\tilde{H}_{\mu}$ is a $\operatorname{poly}(n) \times \operatorname{poly}(n)$ dimension matrix, computing $\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})$ and $\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu} \rVert$ can also be done in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. Therefore, since $m  = \operatorname{poly}(n)$, we can compute $\sup_{\mu \in [m]}\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert$, $\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})$, and $\sup_{\mu \in [m]}|\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time as well, implying we can compute $a'$, $b'$ and each $H_{\mu}$ in a total of $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. Since $|F| = m =\operatorname{poly}(n)$ and we can compute each $H_{\mu} \in F$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, we also can compute the whole set $F$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time as well. Thus we can efficiently construct an instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} from an instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} for $k \leq \log(n)$. \\
    
    \ul{\textbf{Completeness:}} \\
    
    Let $(J, a, b)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} and $(F, a, b, A, B)$ be the instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} constructed according to the description provided above. We require $(F, a, b, A, B)$ to be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} implying there exists pure quantum state $\ket{\psi}\in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ such that
    \begin{equation}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \leq a',
    \end{equation}
    where $H = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m} H_{\mu}$. 

    Since $(J, a, b)$ is an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} there exists an $n$ qubit state $\ket{\psi}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \leq a.
    \end{equation}
    Choose on our doubled Hilbert space the pure quantum state $\ket{\psi}_{A}\otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}$ and thus we choose $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$, we find
    \begin{align}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) &= \left(-(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \mathrm{Op}(\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}) (\ket{\psi}_{A}\otimes\ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &= \left(- \braket{\mathrm{vec}^{-1}(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}), \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\mathrm{vec}^{-1}(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}))} - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &= \left(- \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})| \right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &= \left(|\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})| \right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &\leq \left(a - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu}) |\right)
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from Lemma~\ref{lm:repartL}. Thus 
    \begin{equation}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \leq \left(a - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})| \right) = a'
    \end{equation}
    as required. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Soundness:}} \\

    Let $(J, a, b)$ be a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} and $(F, a, b, A, B)$ be the instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} constructed according to the description provided above. We require $(F, a, b, A, B)$ to be an \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} implying for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ and $\ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}_{B}$,
    \begin{equation}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}) \geq b',
    \end{equation}
    where $H = \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}H_{\mu}$.

    Let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ and $\ket{\phi}\in \mathcal{H}_{B}$ be arbitrary pure quantum states, calculating $(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B})$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:hamtodecay}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}) &= \left(-(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) \mathrm{Op}(\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}) (\ket{\psi}_{A}\otimes\ket{\phi}_{B}) - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &= \left(- \braket{\mathrm{vec}^{-1}(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}), \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\mathrm{vec}^{-1}(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}))} - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                      &= \left(- \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert\tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})| \right)
    \end{align}
    Evaluating $\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})}$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:uuuper}
        \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} + \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}^{\dagger}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\bar{\phi}} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}} + \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\left(\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\bar{\phi}}) - \frac{1}{2}\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \frac{1}{2}\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\Big(- \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} -2 \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}(\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}\ket{\bar{\phi}}) + |\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}|^{2} )\nonumber \\
                                                                               &+ \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}|^{2} - \bra{\psi}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi}) + \frac{1}{2}(|\bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}|^{2}) - \bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}^{*}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\Big(\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} + \braket{\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\mu}(\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} -|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}|^{2}\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                               &= \frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} + \frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} - \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^{m}|\bra{\psi}L_{\mu}\ket{\psi} - \bra{\bar{\phi}}L_{\mu}\ket{\bar{\phi}}|^{2} \nonumber \\
                                                                               &\leq \frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} + \frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}})},
    \end{align}
    which implies
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:negation}
        -\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} \geq -\frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} - \frac{1}{2}\braket{\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\bar{\phi}}\bra{\bar{\phi}})}.
    \end{equation}
    Since $(J, a, b)$ is a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} we have for all $\ket{\chi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\chi}\bra{\chi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\chi}\bra{\chi})}| \geq b
    \end{equation}
    which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:nonabs}
        -\braket{\ket{\chi}\bra{\chi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\chi}\bra{\chi})} \geq b.
    \end{equation}
    because of Lemma~\ref{lm:repartL}. Thus we find using equation~\eqref{eq:negation}
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:bbb}
        -\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\bar{\phi}})} \geq b
    \end{equation}
    Therefore, combining equation~\eqref{eq:bbb} with equation~\eqref{eq:hamtodecay} gives us
    \begin{equation}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}) \geq \left(b - \sum_{\mu=1}^{m}\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})\right) / \sup_{\mu\in[m]}\left(\lVert \tilde{H}_{\mu}\rVert + |\lambda_{0}(\tilde{H}_{\mu})|\right) = b' 
    \end{equation}
    as required.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:LLinQMA}
    For $k \leq \log(n)$, $\textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} \in \mathrm{QMA}$
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:QCSAT}
    Let $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on a proof register $M$ of $n$ qubits and an ancillary register $A$ of $k=\operatorname{poly}(n)$ qubits, decide
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} there exists an $n$ qubit state $\ket{\psi}$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}V^{*}\right) \geq b$
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} for all $n$ qubit states $\ket{\psi}$, $\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}V^{*}\right) \leq a$
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case, where $b-a \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{def:propdiss}
                                                                         
    Let $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on a register $S$. Define a $\lceil \log(T)\rceil$ qubit clock register $C$, the propagation dissipator associated to $V$ is defined as a Lindbladian dissipator $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{C})$ where
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:DpropD}
        \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{prop}}^{(V)}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{t}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(H_{t}\bullet H_{t}^{*} - \frac{1}{2}\left\{H_{t}^{*}H_{t}, \bullet\right\}\right),
    \end{equation}
    where $H_{t} = \left([U_{t+1}]_{S}\otimes \ket{t+1}_{C} - \mathbb{I}_{S} \otimes \ket{t}_{C}\right)\left([U_{t+1}^{*}]_{S}\otimes \bra{t+1}_{C} - \mathbb{I}_{S} \otimes \bra{t}_{C}\right)$.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:propdisker}
    Let $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}} = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}\left[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S}) \otimes \mathrm{span}\left(\left\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\right\}\right)\right]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ is the circuit rotation associated $V$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:A}
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:propdissgap}
    Let $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right) \geq \frac{1}{8T^{4}}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:A}
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{def:QCSATdis}
    Let $(V, b,a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}, define
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:DQCSAT}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}
    \end{equation}
    where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss},
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Dinp}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\bullet) = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left((\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{0}\bra{0}_{C})\bullet (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}) - \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}, \bullet \right\}\right),
    \end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Dout}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\bullet) = (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}) \bullet (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}) - \frac{1}{2}\left\{\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}\otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}, \bullet\right\}, 
    \end{equation}
    with dissipation rates
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:dissrates}
        \begin{cases}
            \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} = T \\
            \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} = 32T^{4} + 8T^{2} \\
            \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \frac{1}{T-2}\left((32kT^{7} + 8kT^{5} + T^{4})^{2} + 1024kT^{9} + 256 k T^{7} + 32 T^{6}\right)
        \end{cases}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lm:psdecayproj}
    Let $\mathcal{L}_{1}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ be Hermitian Lindbladians acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}) = \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} \oplus (\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}})^{\perp}$, define subspace $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \mathrm{span}(\{\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} \})$ which denotes the span of all pure steady states of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$. If $\mathcal{H}_{1} \neq \emptyset$ and $(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) \geq 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}$, then for all $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - \frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}},
    \end{equation}
    where 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:overlap}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} 
    \end{equation}
    denotes the overlap between $\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}$ and
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{ v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})^{\perp} \; | \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{1} \times \mathcal{H}_{1}^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:E}
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lm:properdecay}
    Let $(V, b,a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Let $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ be a pure history state associated to $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \in \mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{A}$, then the decay of $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}$  is given by  
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big) \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:F}
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{def:histsubspace}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}, then we define
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Hprop}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\mathcal{D}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}\}\right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
\label{def:circsubspace}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dinp} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} and $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace}, then we define
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Hqcirc}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} = \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}\}\right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lm:onlyhist}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$. Define subspace $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} using $V$, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $U^{(V)}$ is given in equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:G}
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lm:onlycirc}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$. Define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hqcirc} of Definition~\ref{def:circsubspace} using $V$, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $U^{(V)}$ is given in equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:G}
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lm:DinpKer}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$ and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} using $V$ as well as $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ according to equation~\ref{eq:Dinp} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}} = \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{M}) \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C})].
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ the circuit rotation associated to $V$, is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:C}
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lm:DinpGap}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$ and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} using $V$ as well as $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ according to equation~\ref{eq:Dinp} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2T}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:C}
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lm:DpropLeakage}
    Let $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ with $T > 2$ and $\mathcal{D}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}. Define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} and 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} \; | \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \times \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\},
    \end{equation}
    then the overlap between $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$ and $\mathsf{M}$ is given by
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} \leq \frac{1}{T-1}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:A}
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lm:DinpLeakage}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$ and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} as well as $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ according to equation~\ref{eq:Dinp} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} and $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hqcirc} of Definition~\ref{def:circsubspace}. In addition define
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} \; | \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} \times \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\},
    \end{equation}
    then the overlap between $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}}$ and $\mathsf{M}$ is given by 
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} =0 
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:C}
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:quasihardness}
    \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
To show \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$ we show there exists a reduction from \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} to \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}.

                                            

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}. Our reduction is two steps. From $(Q, b, a)$ we construct an equivalent \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} instance $(V,b,a)$, then we construct our \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} instance $(J, a', b')$. To do this note, we can always transform $Q=Q_{T'-1}Q_{T-2}\cdots Q_{0}$ into an equivalent circuit $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ that outputs the same quantum state at the end of the computation by simply adding identity gates into the circuit $Q$. Thus we transform $(Q, b, a)$ into an equivalent instance $(V, b, a)$ by adding identity gates into the quantum circuit $Q = Q_{T'-1}Q_{T'-2}'\cdots Q_{0}'$ to produce quantum circuit $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ where
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:T}
        T = T' + \frac{2-a}{b-a} + 2
    \end{equation}
    From $(V, b, a)$, let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b,a)}$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. We construct our instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} by letting $J$ be a set of jump operators generating $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ and setting 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:newab}
        \begin{cases}
            a' = 1 - b,\\
            b' = (1 - \frac{1}{T})(1-a) - \frac{1}{T}.
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    Note, we require $b'-a' \geq 1/\operatorname{poly}(n)$ which we confirm below,
    \begin{equation}
        b' - a' = \frac{(b - a)T  - (2 - a)}{T} = \frac{(b-a)(T'+2)}{T' + \frac{2-a}{b-a} + 2} \geq \frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)},
    \end{equation}
    where the inequality follows from $T' = \operatorname{poly}(n)$ and $0 \leq a \leq 1$. Therefore we only require the set of jump operators $J$ to satisfy the conditions of the problem in-order for $(J, a' , b')$ to be a valid instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}.

    According to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ are generated by jump operators 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:JinpJout}
        \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} = \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}\right\}_{i=1}^{k}, \text{ and } \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} = \left\{\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}\right\}
    \end{equation}
    respectively. According to Definition~\ref{def:propdiss} the propagation dissipator $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ is generated by jump operators 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Jprop}
        \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \left\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left([U_{t+1}]_{MA}\otimes \ket{t+1}_{C} - \mathbb{I}_{MA} \otimes \ket{t}_{C}\right)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left([U_{t+1}^{*}]_{MA}\otimes \bra{t+1}_{C} - \mathbb{I}_{MA} \otimes \bra{t}_{C}\right)\right\}_{t=0}^{T-2}.
    \end{equation}
    Thus, re-scaling each of jump operators in the sets $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ by their respective dissipation rates we define,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:rescaledJs}
        \begin{cases}
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\}, \\
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\, \\
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\}
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    which generate $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ respectively. If we set $J$ equal to the set of all jump operators in $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, then $J$ generates $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$. 

    Let $L \in J$, we have $\left\lVertL\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(T, k)$, which follows from each of the jump operators in $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ having an operator norm upper-bounded by a constant, and equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Since $T' = \operatorname{poly}(n)$, equation~\eqref{eq:T} implies $T=\operatorname{poly}(n)$ too. In-addition $k=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, thus $\left\lVertL\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(n)$ as required. Similarly, each $L$ is acts non-trivially on at most $\log(T)$ qubits given that each operator $\ket{t'}\bra{t}_{C}$ acts on $\log(T)$ many qubits. Since we have $T=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, we have that each $L$ acts non-trivially on at most $\log(n)$ qubits implying $J$ generates a $\log(n)$-local Lindbladian dissipator as required. Finally, since both $T=\operatorname{poly}(n)$ and $k=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, there are $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ many jump operators in the set $J$, thus $(J, a', b')$ forms a valid instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}.

       To complete the description of our reduction we require the algorithm that constructs $(J, a' ,b')$ from our instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} $(Q, b, a)$ to be efficient. Equations~\eqref{eq:T} and~\eqref{eq:newab} imply we can compute $a'$ and $b'$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. In-addition, the transformation from $Q$ to $V$ requires only adding $(2 -a) / (b-a) = \operatorname{poly}(n)$ many identity gates into the description of the circuit $Q$ which can also be done in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. Finally, note each of the jump operators in $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ and $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ are matrices of dimension $\operatorname{poly}(n) \times \operatorname{poly}(n)$ and thus can be computed in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time from the dimension $\operatorname{poly}(n) \times \operatorname{poly}(n)$ matrix representations of $\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}$, $\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}$, and $\ket{t'}\bra{t}_{C}$ using standard matrix manipulation algorithms. A similar argument holds for each of the jump operators in $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ since each of the unitary gates $U_{t}$ in the quantum circuit $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ act on at most a constant number of qubits. Since there are $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ many jump operators in $J$, and each $L \in J$ can be computed in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time, the total runtime of the algorithm computing the set of jump operators $J$ from $(V, b, a)$ is $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ which is efficient. Thus there exists an efficient algorithm transforming our instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} to our instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Completeness:}} \\

    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}, and $(J, a', b')$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} generated according to the description above. The jump operators $J$ generate $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined in equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} where $(V, b, a)$ is also an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} since both circuits $Q$ and $V$ output the same quantum state. For completeness, we require $(J, a', b')$ to be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}, which requires there to exist a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \leq a'.
    \end{equation}

    To show this, consider a pure history state $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ associated to the quantum circuit $V$. Choosing $\ket{\phi} = \ket{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A}$ and applying Lemma~\ref{lm:properdecay} we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right)\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                                               &\times\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}) V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
    Since our $(V, b, a)$ forms an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} we can bound 
    \begin{equation}
        0 \leq \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) = 1 - \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) \leq 1 - b,
    \end{equation}
    implying
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{QCSAT}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| \leq 1 - b = a'
    \end{equation}
    as required. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Soundness:}} \\

    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}, and $(J, a', b')$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} generated according to the description above. The jump operators $J$ generate $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined in equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} where $(V, b, a)$ is also an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} since both circuits $Q$ and $V$ output the same quantum state. For soundness, we require $(J, a', b')$ to be an \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} requiring for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$, 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq b'.
    \end{equation}

    To show this let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)} = \mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2}$, where $ \mathcal{L}_{2} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}  + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{1} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$. Since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ is Hermitian along with $\mathcal{L}_{1}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{2}$, we can apply our pure state decay projection lemma, Lemma~\ref{lm:psdecayproj}, finding for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd1}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - \frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}}.
    \end{equation}
    Since $\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} = \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$, $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ where $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace}. Therefore equation~\eqref{eq:lwbd1} becomes for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd2}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}(\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - p_{1}
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:p1}
        p_{1} = \frac{2\left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}},
    \end{equation}
    Letting $\mathcal{L}_{1} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{2} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}$ and applying Lemma~\ref{lm:psdecayproj} again inside $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})$ we find for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd3}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| -\frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}})\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}} - p_{1}.
    \end{equation}
    Note, since we have applied the statement inside $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})$, $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \{\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}\} = \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ where $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hqcirc} of Definition~\ref{def:circsubspace}. Therefore our lower-bound for the decay of an arbitrary pure quantum state $\ket{\psi}$ becomes
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd4}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}(\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})(\ket{h}\bra{h})}|  - p_{1} - p_{2}
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined
    \begin{equation}
        p_{2} =  \frac{2\left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}})\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right\rVert_{\infty}}.
    \end{equation}
    Since for all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$, we have $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$ and $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}$, we can re-write equation~\eqref{eq:lwbd4} giving us for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$, 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd5}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}|  - p_{1} - p_{2}.
    \end{equation}

    Considering the decay of an arbitrary $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$. Lemma~\ref{lm:onlycirc} implies
    we can write $\ket{h} = \ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ where $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ is a pure history state associated to $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi}=\ket{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A}$ for some $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{M}$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lm:properdecay} we find for all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ ,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:circdecay}
        |\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}
        _{A})V^{*}\right)\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                             &\times \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
    Since our $(V, b, a)$ forms a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} we can bound 
    \begin{equation}
        1 \geq \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) = 1 - \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) \geq 1 - a
    \end{equation}
    implying for all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:circdecay1}
        |\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| \geq \left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)(1-a).
    \end{equation}
    Applying the above equation to our lower-bound for the decay of an arbitrary pure quantum state, equation~\eqref{eq:lwbd5}, we find for all pure states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd6}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)(1 - a)  - p_{1} - p_{2}.
    \end{equation}


    Moving to calculating our perturbations $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$. From Lemma~\ref{lm:Lupperbound} and equations~\eqref{eq:Dinp} \eqref{eq:Dout} and~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:norms}
        \begin{cases}
            \left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq 2\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} \\
            \left\lVert\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty}  \leq 2(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})
        \end{cases} .
    \end{equation}
    In-addition, from Proposition~\ref{prop:propdissgap} and Lemma~\ref{lm:DpropLeakage} as well as Lemma~\ref{lm:DinpGap} and Lemma~\ref{lm:DinpLeakage} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:gaps+leakage}
        \begin{cases}
            (1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right) \geq \left(1 - \frac{1}{T-1}\right)\frac{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}{8T^{4}} \geq \frac{(T-2)\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}{8T^{5}} \\
            (1 - \cos^{2}\theta_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}})\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}\right) \geq \frac{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}{2T}
        \end{cases} .
    \end{equation}
    Thus for $p_{1}$ we calculate
    \begin{align}
        p_{1} &\leq \frac{8(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})^{2}}{\frac{(T-2)\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}{8T^{5}}- 4(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})} = \frac{1}{2T}
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from the definitions of $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, and $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ provided in equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. For perturbation $p_{2}$ we calculate
    \begin{equation}
        p_{2} \leq  \frac{8\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}^{2}}{\frac{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}{2T} - 4\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}}
 = \frac{1}{2T}
    \end{equation}
    where the last equality follows from our definitions of $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ and $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ provided in equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Applying our upper-bounds on $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$ to equation~\eqref{eq:lwbd6} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lwbd7}
        |\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| \geq   \left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)(1-a) - \frac{1}{T} = b'.
    \end{equation}
    as required.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Complete}$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Consider the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness} and the set of jump operators $J$ used to form the $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}. For all $L \in J$, it follows from equations~\eqref{eq:JinpJout} \eqref{eq:Jprop} and \eqref{eq:rescaledJs} that $L = L^{*}$. Thus the $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard instance of \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} is also a valid instance of \textsc{Hermitian $\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian}. Therefore \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard using the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness}.

    In our instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} $(Q, b, a)$ in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness} set $b=1$. Thus \textsc{Hermitian $\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian} with $a=0$ is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-Hard. From Proposition~\ref{prop:rlltollps} of Section~\ref{sec:dfs} we find \textsc{$\log(n)$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-Hard.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{def:localDQCSAT}
    Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ be defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ be the modification of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ under the mapping defined in equation~\eqref{eq:local}, then the local \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} dissipator is defined as
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Dloc}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} + \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)},
    \end{equation}
    where 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Dunary}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\sum_{x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}\left(\frac{1}{4}(\ket{x}\bra{y}_{t+2,t+1,t}) \bullet (\ket{y}\bra{x}_{t+2,t+1,t}) - \frac{1}{8}\left\{\ket{y}\bra{y}_{t+2,t+1,t}, \bullet \right\}\right),
    \end{equation}
    with $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:localillandlegstrings} and dissipation rate
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Gunary}
        \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} = \frac{100T^{4}}{(T-1)}\left[4(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + T \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}) + 8T(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + T \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})^{2}\right]
    \end{equation}
    where $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, and $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ are defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lm:properdecayloc}
    Let $(V, b,a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}.  Let $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ be a pure history state associated to $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi} = \ket{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \in \mathcal{H}_{M}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{A}$, then the decay of $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}$  is given by  
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big) \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:F}
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:DuKer}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and $P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ be the projection onto $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ with $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:globalillandlegsubspaces} , then 
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}} = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA}) \otimes \left(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}) \oplus P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\right)
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:D}
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:DuGap}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}, then 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) = 1 / 96T^{3}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:D}
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lm:DuLeakage}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:globalillandlegsubspaces} and
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} \; \big| \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)} \times [\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}]^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\},
    \end{equation}
    then the overlap between $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}$ and $\mathsf{M}$ is given by 
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}, A \in \mathsf{M} \\ \braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = \braket{A, A} = 1}} |\braket{A_{0}, A}|^{2} \leq \frac{1}{2^{T} - T}
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:D}
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:localhardness}
    For $k \geq 5$, \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
To show \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$ we show there exists a reduction from \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} to \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} for $k \geq 5$.\\

                                            

    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}. Similar to our reduction in Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness}, from $(Q, b, a)$ we construct an instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} by transforming the \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} instance $(Q,b,a)$ into an equivalent instance $(V,b,a)$ then into the \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} instance $(J, a', b')$ for $k \geq 5$. Similarly, to transform $(Q, b, a)$ into an equivalent instance $(V, b, a)$ we add identity gates into the quantum circuit $Q = Q_{T'-1}Q_{T'-2}\cdots Q_{0}$ to produce quantum circuit $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ where
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Tlocal}
        T = T' + \frac{3-a}{b-a} + 2.
    \end{equation}
    From \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} instance $(V, b, a)$, let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b,a)}$ be the local \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} dissipator defined in equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}. We construct our instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} by letting $J$ be a set of jump operators which generate $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ and setting 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:abloc}
        \begin{cases}
            a' = 1 - b,\\
            b' = (1 - \frac{1}{T})(1-a) - \frac{2}{T}.
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
