    Similar to our proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness} we confirm,
    \begin{equation}
        b' - a' = \frac{(b - a)T  - (3 - a)}{T} = \frac{(b-a)(T' + 2)}{T' + \frac{3-a}{b-a} + 2} \geq \frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)}. 
    \end{equation}
    Thus we only require the set of jump operators $J$ to satisfy the conditions of the problem in-order for $(J, a' , b')$ to be a valid instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian}.


    According to equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}, $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} + \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ is generated by jump operators 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Junary}
        \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} = \left\{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}(\ket{x}\bra{y}_{t+2,t+1,t} +  \ket{y}\bra{x}_{t+2,t+1,t}), \frac{i}{2\sqrt{2}}(\ket{x}\bra{y}_{t+2,t+1,t} -  \ket{y}\bra{x}_{t+2,t+1,t})\; \Big| \; x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}\right\}_{t=0}^{T-3}
    \end{equation}
    and $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ is equal to $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ after having applied the mapping of equation~\eqref{eq:local}. $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V,b,a)}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} implies we can write $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ where $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, and $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$  are equal to $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$, and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ of equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} after having applied the mapping of equation~\eqref{eq:local}. Thus we find that $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ and $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ can be generated by jump operators
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:JinpandJoutlocal}
        \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} = \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{1}\right\}_{i=1}^{k}, \text{ and } \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} = \left\{\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{1}\bra{1}_{T-1}\right\}
    \end{equation}
    respectively, along with $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ being generated by jump operators
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:Jproplocal}
        \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \Big\{ \frac{1}{2}\big(\ket{01}\bra{01}_{t+2, t+1} -& [U_{t+1}]_{MA} \otimes \ket{011}\bra{001}_{t+2,t+1,t} \nonumber \\
        &- [U^{*}_{t+1}]_{MA} \otimes \ket{001}\bra{011}_{t+2,t+1,t} + \ket{01}\bra{01}_{t+1,t}\big)\Big\}_{t=0}^{T-2}.
    \end{align}
    Re-scaling each set of jump operators according to their respective dissipation rates we can define jump operator sets 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:jumpslocal}
        \begin{cases}
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\}, \\
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\}, \\
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\}, \\
            J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = \{\sqrt{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}L \; | \; L \in \tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\} 
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    which generate $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$, $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ respectively. Thus $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ can be generated by the set of jump operators $J$, equal to the set of all jump operators contained in the sets $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$, $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$, and $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$.

    Note, each of the jump operators in $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$, $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ and $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ have an operator norm upper-bounded by a constant. In-addition, all of the dissipation rates are $\operatorname{poly}(T, k)$, thus for all $L \in J$ we have $\left\lVertL\right\rVert \leq \operatorname{poly}(n)$. We also find, since each of the jump operators in $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$, $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, and $\tilde{J}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ act on $k\leq 3$ qubits, each of the jump operators in $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$, $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$, and $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ also act on $k\leq 3$ qubits. Since each gate $U_{t}$ in our quantum circuit $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ acts on $k \geq 2$, we find that each jump operator in $J_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ acts on $k \geq 5$ qubits. Thus for all $L \in J$, the jump operator $L$ acts non-trivially on at most $k$ qubits for $k \geq 5$ as required. In-addition, since $T=\operatorname{poly}(n)$ and $k=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, we have $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ many jump operators in $J$. Thus$(J, a', b')$ forms a valid instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} for $k \geq 5$.

    To complete our description of the reduction we require the existence of an efficient algorithm that can construct $(J, a' ,b')$ from our instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} $(Q, b, a)$. Equations~\eqref{eq:Tlocal} and~\eqref{eq:abloc} imply we can compute $a'$ and $b'$ in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. In-addition, the transformation from $Q$ to $V$ only requires adding $[(3 - a) / (b-a)] + 2= \operatorname{poly}(n)$ many identity gates into the description of the circuit $Q$ which can also be done in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time. Since each of the jump operators in $J$ are $k$-local for a constant $k\geq 5$, they can be represented as matrices of constant dimension and can be computed in constant time from the matrix representations of their various components. Since there are $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ many jump operators in $J$, the total runtime of the algorithm computing the set of jump operators $J$ from $(V, b, a)$ is $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ which is efficient. Thus there exists an efficient algorithm transforming an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} to an instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} for $k\geq 5$. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Completeness:}} \\

    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}, and $(J, a', b')$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} generated according to the description above. The jump operators $J$ generate $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined in equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} where $(V, b, a)$ is also an \emph{(accept-case)} instance \textsc{Qunatum Circuit-SAT}. For completeness, we require $(J, a', b')$ to be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} implying there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \leq a'.
    \end{equation}

    To show this, consider a pure history state $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ associated to $V$. Choosing $\ket{\phi}_{MA} = \ket{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A}$ and applying Lemma~\ref{lm:properdecayloc} we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right)\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                                               &\times \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}) V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
    Since our $(V, b, a)$ forms an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} we can bound 
    \begin{equation}
        0 \leq \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) = 1 - \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{M_{0}}V(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A})V^{*}\right) \leq 1 - b,
    \end{equation}
    implying
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| \leq  1 - b = a'
    \end{equation}
    as required. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Soundness:}} \\

    Let $(Q, b, a)$ be a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}, and $(J, a', b')$ be the corresponding instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} generated according to the description above. The jump operators $J$ generate $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined in equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} with $(V, b, a)$ being also a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT}. For soundness, we require $(J, a', b')$ to be a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} implying for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$, 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq b'.
    \end{equation}

    To show this let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)} = \mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2}$, where $ \mathcal{L}_{2} = \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{1} = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lm:psdecayproj} we find for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:prjtounary}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}}&|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - \frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}} 
    \end{align}
    where $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{\psi}\in\mathcal{H} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}\}\right)$. Since $\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} = \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}$, we can apply Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} implying $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ where $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:globalillandlegsubspaces}. Therefore equation~\eqref{eq:prjtounary} becomes for all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prjtounary1}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - p_{u}
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:pu}
        p_{u} = \frac{2\left\lVert \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)} \right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) - 2\left\lVert \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)} \right\rVert_{\infty}}
    \end{equation}

    Proceeding to evaluate $p_{u}$, from Lemma~\ref{lm:Lupperbound} and Definitions~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and~\ref{def:QCSATdis} we find
    \begin{align}
        \left\lVert\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V,b,a)}\right\rVert_{\infty} &\leq \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\left\lVert\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\left\lVert\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right\rVert_{\infty} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} \left\lVert\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} \nonumber \\
                                                &\leq 2(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}  + T\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}).
    \end{align}
    From Proposition~\ref{prop:DuGap} and Lemma~\ref{lm:DuLeakage} we find
    \begin{equation}
        (1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) \geq  \left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)\frac{\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}{100T^{3}} = \frac{(T-1)\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}{100T^{4}}
    \end{equation}
    Thus upper-bounding $p_{u}$ using the above equation we find
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:pu1}
        p_{u} \leq \frac{8(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + T\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})^{2}}{\frac{(T-1)}{100T^{4}}\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} - 4(k\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} + T\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}})} \leq  \frac{1}{T}
    \end{equation}
    where the last inequality follows from applying our definition of $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ found in equation~\eqref{eq:Gunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}. Thus from equation~\eqref{eq:prjtounary1} we find for all pure states $\ket{\psi}$, 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prjtounary2}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| - \frac{1}{T}.
    \end{equation}
    Note, inside $\mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$, we can reverse the mapping described in equation~\eqref{eq:local} given that both sides of the mapping act on the basis of $\mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ in the same way. Reversing the mapping described in equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary}, allows us to map $\mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ back to $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{old}}$ which is defined as the Hilbert space our original quasi-local dissipator of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} acts on. Therefore the first term in the lower-bound of equation~\eqref{eq:prjtounary2} can be bounded as
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:oldanalysis}
        \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{old}}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}|
    \end{equation}
    where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Applying equation~\eqref{eq:lwbd7} found in our proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:quasihardness} we find, for all pure states $\ket{\psi}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prjtounary3}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \left(1 - \frac{1}{T}\right)(1-a) - \frac{2}{T} = b' 
    \end{equation}
    as required.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
For $k \geq 5$, \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-$\mathrm{Complete}$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
For $k \geq 5$, \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-$\mathrm{Hard}$
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Consider the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:localhardness} and the set of jump operators $J$ used to form the $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian}. For all $L \in J$, it follows from equations~\eqref{eq:Junary}, \eqref{eq:JinpandJoutlocal}, \eqref{eq:Jproplocal}, and \eqref{eq:jumpslocal} that $L = L^{*}$. Thus the $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard instance of \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian} is also a valid instance of \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian}. Therefore for $k \geq 5$, \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} is $\mathrm{QMA}$-Hard using the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:localhardness}.

    In our instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} $(Q, b, a)$ in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:localhardness} set $b=1$. Thus for $k \geq 5$, \textsc{Hermitian $k$-Local Lindbladian} with $a=0$ is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-Hard. From Proposition~\ref{prop:rlltollps} of Section~\ref{sec:dfs} we find for $k \geq 5$, \textsc{$k$-Local Lindbladian Pure Steady-State} is $\mathrm{QMA}_{1}$-Hard.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lm:rotpropdef}
    Let $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}. Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ be the  circuit rotation for $V$, then
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:lmrot}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}(\bullet) = \mathcal{I}_{S} \otimes \left[\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C} \bullet \ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C} - \frac{1}{2}\left\{\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C}, \bullet \right\}\right)\right],
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{-_{t}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\ket{t} - \ket{t+1})$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Proceeding by direct calculation we find
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\tilde{H}_{t}\bullet \tilde{H}_{t}^{*} - \frac{1}{2}\left\{\tilde{H}_{t}^{*}\tilde{H}_{t}, \bullet\right\}\right)
    \end{equation}
    where
    \begin{align}
        \tilde{H}_{t} &= \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(H_{t}) = \left(\sum_{t'=0}^{T-1}[V_{t'}]_{S}\otimes \ket{t'}\bra{t'}_{C}\right)^{*}H_{t} \left(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}[V_{t''}]_{S}\otimes \ket{t''}\bra{t''}_{C}\right) \\
                      &= \frac{1}{2}([V^{*}_{t+1}U_{t+1}]_{S} \otimes \ket{t+1}_{C} - [V_{t}]_{S}^{*}\otimes\ket{t}_{C})([V^{*}_{t+1}U_{t+1}]_{S}^{*} \otimes \bra{t+1}_{C} - [V_{t}]_{S}\otimes\bra{t}_{C}) \\
                      &= \frac{1}{2}\left([V_{t}]_{S}^{*}\otimes (\ket{t+1}_{C} - \ket{t}_{C})\right)\left([V_{t}]_{S}\otimes(\bra{t+1}_{C} - \bra{t}_{C})\right) =  \mathbb{I}_{S} \otimes \ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}.
    \end{align}
    The result then follows.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lm:rotadistograph}
    Let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be the rotated propagation dissipator and define a basis for $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})$ given by
    \begin{equation}
        \{P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})} \; | \; (t_{A}, t_{B}) \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-1\}\} \text{ where } P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})} = \ket{t_{A}}\bra{t_{B}}.
    \end{equation}
    Let $L$ be the matrix defined by elements
    \begin{equation}
        L_{v_{1},v_{2}} = -4\braket{P_{v_{1}}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{v_{2}})} \text{ for } v_{1}, v_{2} \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-1\}^{\times 2},
    \end{equation}
    then $L$ is a Laplacian for a graph $G$ with vertices $V = \{0, 1,\cdots, T-1\}^{\times 2}$.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Let $(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V$, calculating the matrix element of $L$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:part1}
        L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} &= -4\braket{P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})'}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})})} = -4\braket{\ket{t_{A}'}\bra{t_{B}'}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{t_{A}}\bra{t_{B}})} \nonumber \\
                                            &= -4\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{A}}\braket{t_{B}|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'} - \frac{1}{2}\braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}}\delta_{t_{B},t_{B}'} - \frac{1}{2}\braket{t'_{B}|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}}\delta_{t_{A}, t_{A}'}\right).
    \end{align}
    Given that $\ket{-_{t}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\ket{t} - \ket{t-1})$, we find $L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} \in \mathbb{R}$. Taking the transpose of $L$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:intercal}
        [L^{\intercal}]_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} &= L_{(t_{A}, t_{B}), (t_{A}, t_{B})'} = -4\braket{P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})'})} = -4 \overline{\braket{P_{(t_{A},t_{B})'}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\dagger}(P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})})}} \nonumber \\
                                                          &= -4 \overline{\braket{P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})'}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})})}} = \overline{L}_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} = L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})}, 
    \end{align}
    where the second line follows from $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\dagger} = \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$. Equation~\eqref{eq:intercal} implies,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prop1}
        L^{\intercal} = L.
    \end{equation}

    Let $(t_{A}, t_{B})' \neq (t_{A}, t_{B})$, which implies three cases
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $(t_{A} \neq t_{A}')$ and $(t_{B} = t_{B}')$
        \item $(t_{A} = t_{A}')$ and $(t_{B} \neq t_{B}')$
        \item $(t_{A} \neq t_{A}')$ and $(t_{B} \neq t_{B}')$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Consider the first of the three cases given above, applying equation~\eqref{eq:part1} we find, 
    \begin{align}
        L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} &= 2 \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\braket{t_{A}' | -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}}(1 - 2|\braket{t_{B}| -_{t}}|^{2})\Big) = 2 \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\braket{t_{A}' | -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}}(1 - |\delta_{t_{B},t} - \delta_{t_{B},t+1}|^{2})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                            &= \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big((\delta_{t_{A}', t} - \delta_{t_{A}', t+1})(\delta_{t_{A},t} - \delta_{t_{A},t+1})(1 - \delta_{t_{B},t} - \delta_{t_{B},t+1})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                            &= - \delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'+1}(1 - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1}) - \delta_{t_{A}',t_{A}+1}(1 - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}+1})
    \end{align}
    Note, for all $(t_{A}, t_{B})$ and $(t_{A}, t_{B})'$ both $(1 - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1})$ and $(1 - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}+1})$ take values only in the set $\{0, 1\}$ implying $L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} \in \{0, -1\}$.  
    Consider the second of the three cases, similarly, we find
    \begin{align}
        L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} &= 2 \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\braket{t_{B}' | -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{B}}(1 - 2|\braket{t_{A}| -_{t}}|^{2})\Big) = 2 \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\braket{t_{B}' | -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{B}}(1 - |\delta_{t_{A},t} - \delta_{t_{A},t+1}|^{2})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                            &= \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big((\delta_{t_{B}', t} - \delta_{t_{B}', t+1})(\delta_{t_{B},t} - \delta_{t_{B},t+1})(1 - \delta_{t_{A},t} - \delta_{t_{A},t+1})\Big) \nonumber \\
                                            &= - \delta_{t_{B},t_{B}'+1}(1 - \delta_{t_{A},t_{B}'} - \delta_{t_{A},t_{B}'+1}) - \delta_{t_{B}',t_{B}+1}(1 - \delta_{t_{A},t_{B}} - \delta_{t_{A},t_{B}+1}) \in \{0, -1\}.
    \end{align}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
    Finally, consider the third of the three cases discussed above, we find 
    \begin{align}
        L_{(t_{A},t_{B})', (t_{A},t_{B})} &= -4\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}}\braket{t_{B}| -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'} \nonumber \\
                                          &= -\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\left((\delta_{t_{A}',t} - \delta_{t_{A}', t+1})(\delta_{t_{A},t} - \delta_{t_{A},t+1})(\delta_{t_{B},t} - \delta_{t_{B},t+1})(\delta_{t_{B}',t} - \delta_{t_{B}',t+1})\right) \nonumber \\
                                          &= \delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'+1}(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1})(\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'} - \delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'+1}) + \delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'-1}(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'-1} - \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'})(\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'-1} - \delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'}) \nonumber \\
                                          &= -\delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'+1}(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'+1} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'}) - \delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'-1}(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'-1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'-1}).
    \end{align}
    The equation above implies 
    \begin{equation}
        L_{(t_{A},t_{B})', (t_{A},t_{B})} = \begin{cases}-(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'+1} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'}) \text{ for } t_{A} = t_{A}'+1  \\ - (\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'-1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'-1}) \text{ for } t_{A} = t_{A}'-1 \\ 0 \text{ otherwise }.
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    It is clear that $(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'+1} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'+1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'}) \in \{0, 1\}$; similarly, $(\delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'-1}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'} + \delta_{t_{B},t_{A}'}\delta_{t_{B}',t_{A}'-1}) \in \{0, 1\}$. Therefore we have $L_{(t_{A},t_{B})', (t_{A},t_{B})} \in \{0, -1\}$.  Thus we find for all $v_{1}, v_{2} \in V$ and $v_{1} \neq v_{2}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prop2}
        L_{v_{1}, v_{2}} \in \{0, -1\}
    \end{equation}


    Consider the sum $\sum_{(t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V} L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})}$, applying equation~\eqref{eq:part1}, we find,
    \begin{align}
        \sum_{(t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V} L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A}, t_{B})} &= 2\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\sum_{(t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V}\big(\braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}}(\delta_{t_{B},t_{B}'} - \braket{t_{B}| -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'})\big) \nonumber \\
                                                                        &\quad + \sum_{(t_{A},t_{B})\in V}\big(\braket{t_{B}|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'}(\delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'} - \braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}})\big)\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                                        &= \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\sum_{(t_{A}, t_{B})\in V}\big(\braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}(\delta_{t,t_{A}} - \delta_{t+1,t_{A}})(\delta_{t_{B},t_{B}'} - \braket{t_{B}| -_{t}}\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'})\big) \nonumber \\
                                                                        &\quad + \sum_{(t_{A},t_{B})\in V}\big(\braket{-_{t}|t_{B}'}(\delta_{t,t_{B}} - \delta_{t+1,t_{B}})(\delta_{t_{A},t_{A}'} - \braket{t_{A}'|-_{t}}\braket{-_{t}| t_{A}} )\big)\Big) .
    \end{align} 
    Note, $\sum_{t_{A}=0}^{T-1}(\delta_{t,t_{A}} - \delta_{t+1,t_{A}}) = \sum_{t_{B}=0}^{T-1}(\delta_{t,t_{B}} - \delta_{t+1,t_{B}}) =0$ for all $0 \leq t < T-1$, therefore
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:prop3}
        \sum_{(t_{A},t_{B}) \in V} L_{(t_{A}, t_{B})', (t_{A},t_{B})} = 0.
    \end{equation}

    Given that matrix $L$ satisfies equations~\eqref{eq:prop1},~\eqref{eq:prop2}, and~\eqref{eq:prop3} we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:mattograph} of Appendix~\ref{app:B} implying $L$ is a Laplacian for a graph $G$ over vertices $V$. The statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} follows.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lm:mixcomp}
    Let $G$ be the graph defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} and $G_{m}$ be the subgraph associated to vertices $V_{m} = \{(t,t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$, $G_{m}$ is a connected component of $G$.
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:B}
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lm:purecomp}
    Let $G$ be the graph defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} and $G_{p}$ be the subgraph associated to vertices $V_{p} = V \setminus \{(t, t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$, $G_{p}$ is a connected component of $G$.
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
See Appendix~\ref{app:B}
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:comps}
    Let $G$ be the graph defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph}, then $G$ has only two connected components.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lm:kerrotprop}
    Let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be the rotated propagation dissipator, then
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}} = \mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right)
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}_{C}$.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Consider the action 
    \begin{equation}
        \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}) =  \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\ket{-_{t}}_{C}\braket{-_{t}|p}\braket{p|-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C} - \frac{1}{2}\left\{\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} \right\}\right),
    \end{equation}
    calculating $\braket{p|-_{t}}$ we find
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{p|-_{t}}  = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sum_{t'=0}^{T-1}(\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1}) = 0 \text{ for all } t\in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-2\}, 
    \end{equation}
    thus $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}) = 0$  implying $\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} \in \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}$. Similarly,
    \begin{equation}
        \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\mathbb{I}_{C}) =  \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\ket{-_{t}}_{C}\braket{-_{t}|-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C} - \frac{1}{2}\left\{\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}_{C}, \mathbb{I}_{C} \right\}\right) = 0,
    \end{equation}
    therefore $\mathbb{I}_{C} \in \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}$. The set $\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}\}$ is linearly independent, thus $\dim\mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right) = 2$, in addition $\mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right) \subseteq \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}$. 

    Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} implies $\dim\ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}} = \dim\ker{L_{G}}$ where $L_{G}$ is the Laplacian associated to graph $G$ defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph}. The algebraic multiplicity of the zero eigenvalue of $L_{G}$ is equal to the $\dim\ker{L_{G}}$, thus applying Theorem 3.10 of \cite{marsden2013eigenvalues} implies $\dim\ker{L_{G}}$ is equal to the number of connected components of graph $G$. Thus we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \dim\ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}} = \dim\ker{L_{G}} = 2,
    \end{equation}
    following from Corollary~\ref{cor:comps}. Assume $\mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right)$ is strictly a subspace of $\ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}$. We require
    \begin{equation}
        \dim\mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right) < \dim\ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}
    \end{equation}
    but clearly $\dim\mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right) = 2= \dim\ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}$ which is a contradiction. Thus,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right) = \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}}
    \end{equation}
    must hold.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proposition--1: body_md -->
Let $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}} = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}\left[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S}) \otimes \mathrm{span}\left(\left\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\right\}\right)\right]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ is the circuit rotation associated to $V$.
<!-- end proposition--1 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ be the circuit rotation for quantum circuit $V$ acting on $\mathcal{H}_{MA}$ and let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be the rotated propagation dissipator. Lemma~\ref{lm:rotpropdef} implies
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)} = \mathcal{I}_{S} \otimes \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}},
    \end{equation}
    which further implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:rotatedker}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}} = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S}) \otimes \ker{\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}} = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S}) \otimes \mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right)
    \end{equation}
    where the last equality follows from Lemma~\ref{lm:kerrotprop}. The statement of Proposition~\ref{prop:propdisker} follows.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lm:gaprotprop}
    Let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be the rotated propagation dissipator, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T(T-1)}\right)\right).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
From Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} we directly have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) = \frac{1}{4}\mathrm{gap}\left(L_{G}\right)
    \end{equation}
    where $L_{G}$ is the Laplacian of the graph $G$ defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph}. Applying part (vi) of Lemma 1.7 from \cite{chung1997spectral} as well as Corollary~\ref{cor:comps} implies $\mathrm{Sp}\left(L_{G}\right) = \mathrm{Sp}\left(L_{G_{m}}\right) \cup \mathrm{Sp}\left(L_{G_{p}}\right)$. Thus we can write,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:graphcomps}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) = \frac{1}{4}\inf\left\{\mathrm{gap}\left(L_{G_{m}}\right) , \mathrm{gap}\left(L_{G_{p}}\right) \right\}
    \end{equation}


    Let $\lambda_{i}(A)$ denote the $i$-th eigenvalue of Hermitian operator $A$, ordered according to $\lambda_{0}(A) \leq \lambda_{1}(A) \leq \cdots \lambda_{i}(A) \leq \cdots$. Lemmas~\ref{lm:mixcomp} and~\ref{lm:purecomp} imply subgraphs $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ are connected components. Applying part (iv) of Lemma 1.7 from \cite{chung1997spectral} allows us to simplify equation~\eqref{eq:graphcomps} as 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) = \frac{1}{4}\inf\left\{\lambda_{1}(L_{G_{m}}), \lambda_{1}(L_{G_{p}})\right\}.
    \end{equation}
    Applying Theorem 6.1 of \cite{zhang2011laplacian} allows us to lower-bound $\lambda_{1}(L_{G_{m}})$ and $\lambda_{1}(L_{G_{p}})$ since $G_{p}$ and $G_{m}$ are simple connected graphs. We find 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2}\min\left\{\kappa'(G_{m})\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{|V_{m}|}\right)\right), \kappa'(G_{p})\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{|V_{p}|}\right)\right) \right\},
    \end{equation}
    where $V_{m}$ and $V_{p}$ denote the sets of vertices associated to graphs $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ respectively, and $\kappa'(G)$ denotes the edge-connectivity of graph $G$. From the definitions of the graphs $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ found in Lemmas~\ref{lm:mixcomp} and~\ref{lm:purecomp} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{cases}
            |V_{m}| = |\{(t,t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}| = T   \\
            |V_{p}| = |\{(t_{A}, t_{B})\}_{t_{A}, t_{B}=0}^{T-1}| - |V_{m}| = T(T-1),
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    Since both graphs $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ are connected according to Lemmas~\ref{lm:mixcomp} and~\ref{lm:purecomp} respectively we have
    \begin{equation}
        1 \leq \kappa'(G_{m}), \kappa'(G_{p}).
    \end{equation}
    Therefore we find
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2}\min\left\{\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T}\right)\right), \left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T(T-1)}\right)\right) \right\}.
    \end{equation}
    For $T > 1$, we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T(T-1)}\right)\right)
    \end{equation}
    and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:gaprotprop} follows.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proposition--2: body_md -->
Let $V = U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right) \geq \frac{1}{8T^{4}}
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition--2 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ be the circuit rotation for $V$ and let $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be the rotated propagation dissipator. Lemma~\ref{lm:rotpropdef} allows us to write
    \begin{align}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right) &= \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)} \circ \mathcal{I}_{S} \otimes \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}\right) = \mathrm{gap}\left(\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T(T-1)}\right)\right)
    \end{align}
    where the second equality follows from $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)} \circ \bullet \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}$ being a similarity transformation and thus spectrum preserving and the final inequality from Lemma~\ref{lm:gaprotprop}. For $T > 1$ we can write
    \begin{align}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}\right)  &\geq \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{T(T-1)}\right)\right) \geq \frac{1}{8T^{4}}
    \end{align}
    implying the statement.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- lemma--1: body_md -->
Let $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ be a quantum circuit acting on register $S$ with $T > 2$ and $\mathcal{D}^{(V)}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ be its propagation dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DpropD} of Definition~\ref{def:propdiss}. Define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} and 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} \; | \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \times \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\},
    \end{equation}
    then the overlap between $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$ and $\mathsf{M}$ is given by
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} \leq \frac{1}{T-1}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma--1 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ be the circuit rotation associated to $V$. Calculating the overlap we find 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:cos}
        \cos^{2}\theta &= \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(A_{0}),\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(A)}|^{2} \nonumber \\ \\
                       &= \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}], A \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathsf{M}]\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}}|\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2}.
    \end{align}
    From Proposition~\ref{prop:propdisker} we have
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}] = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{S})\otimes \mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right)
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$. Therefore for all $A_{0} \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}]$ we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:finalA0}
        A_{0} = B_{S} \otimes (\mathbb{I}_{C} - \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}) + C_{S} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} = B_{S} \otimes P^{(\perp)}_{C} + C_{S} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C},
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined the projection onto the orthogonal complement to the subspace $\ket{p}_{C}$ as $P^{(\perp)}$. For $A_{0} \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}$ and $\braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} =1$ we find
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = \braket{B, B}\braket{P^{(\perp)}, P^{(\perp)}} + \braket{C,C}\braket{\ket{p}\bra{p},\ket{p}\bra{p}} = \braket{B, B}(T - 1) + \braket{C, C}  = 1.
    \end{equation}
    which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:upperonB}
        \begin{cases}
            \braket{B, B} \leq 1 / (T - 1) \\
            \braket{C, C} \leq 1 
        \end{cases}.
    \end{equation}
                                                          
                     
                            
                                            
                   
    
    Similarly we have for all $A \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathsf{M}]$, 
    \begin{align}
        A &= v_{1}\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(\ket{h}\bra{\perp}) + v_{2} \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(\ket{\perp}\bra{h}) + v_{3}\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}(\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}) \\
          &= v_{1}U^{(V)*}\ket{h}\bra{\perp}U^{(V)} + v_{2} U^{(V)*} \ket{\perp}\bra{h}U^{(V)} + v_{3}U^{(V)*}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}U^{(V)}
    \end{align}
    where $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ and $\ket{\perp} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp}$. Since Lemma~\ref{lm:onlyhist} implies $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = U[\mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}]$ we have $U^{(V)*}\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}$. Thus we can write $A \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathsf{M}]$ as 
    \begin{align}
        A = v_{1}(\ket{\phi}_{S}\otimes\ket{p}_{C})\bra{\perp}U^{(V)} + v_{2} U^{(V)*} \ket{\perp}(\bra{\phi}_{S}\otimes \bra{p}_{C}) + v_{3}U^{(V)*}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}U^{(V)},
    \end{align}
    for some $\ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}_{S}$. To begin analyzing $U^{(V)*}\ket{\perp} \in U^{(V)*}[\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp}] $ note that since $U^{(V)*}$ is a unitary and $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp}$ is the orthogonal complement of $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ we have 
    \begin{equation}
        U^{(V)*}[\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{\perp}] = U^{(V)*}[\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}]^{\perp} = (\mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C})^{\perp} = \mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}^{\perp},
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p}^{\perp}_{C}$ denotes the subspace of $\mathcal{H}_{C}$ which is the orthogonal complement of the subspace $\ket{p}_{C}$. Therefore we can write $A \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathsf{M}]$ as 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:finalA}
        A = v_{1}(\ket{\phi}_{S}\otimes\ket{p}_{C})\bra{\perp'} + v_{2} \ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S}\otimes \bra{p}_{C}) + v_{3}\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'},
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{\perp'} = U^{(V)*}\ket{\perp} \in \mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}^{\perp}$.

    Moving back to calculating $\cos^{2}\theta$, Applying equations~\eqref{eq:finalA0} and~\eqref{eq:finalA}, for all $A_{0} \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}]$ and $A \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathsf{M}]$ such that $\braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = \braket{A, A} = 1$ we have 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} =  |\braket{B_{S}\otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)} + C_{S}\otimes\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}, v_{1}(\ket{\phi}_{S}\otimes\ket{p}_{C})\bra{\perp'} + v_{2} \ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S}\otimes \bra{p}_{C}) + v_{3}\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}}|^{2}
    \end{equation}
    which gives us six terms inside the absolute value. Calculating four of these six terms gives us
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{cases}
            \braket{B_{S}\otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)}, (\ket{\phi}_{S}\otimes\ket{p}_{C})\bra{\perp'}} = \operatorname{Tr}((B_{S}^{*}\ket{\phi}_{S} \otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)}\ket{p}) \bra{\perp'}) = 0 \\
            \braket{B_{S}\otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)}, \ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S} \otimes \bra{p}_{C})} =  \operatorname{Tr}((B_{S}^{*} \otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)})\ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S} \otimes \bra{p}_{C})) = \operatorname{Tr}(\ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S}B_{S}^{*} \otimes \bra{p}_{C}P_{C}^{(\perp)})) = 0 \\
            \braket{C_{S} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}, (\ket{\phi}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C})\bra{\perp'}} = \bra{\perp'}((C^{*}\ket{\phi})_{S}\otimes \ket{p}_{C}) = \bra{\perp}U^{(V)}(\ket{C^{*}\phi}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}) = \braket{\perp|\eta_{C^{*}\phi}} = 0  \\
        \braket{C_{S} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}, \ket{\perp'}(\bra{\phi}_{S}\otimes\bra{p}_{C})} = ((\bra{\phi}C^{*})_{S} \otimes \bra{p}_{C}) \ket{\perp'} = (\bra{C\phi}_{S} \otimes \bra{p}_{C})U^{(V)*}\ket{\perp} = \braket{\eta_{C\phi}|\perp} = 0.
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    Therefore we can write 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} =  |v_{3}|^{2}|\braket{B_{S}\otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)} + C_{S}\otimes\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}, \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}}|^{2}.
    \end{equation}
    Calculating $\braket{C_{S}\otimes\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}, \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}}$ we find
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{C_{S}\otimes\ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}, \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}} = \bra{\perp'}(C_{S} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C})\ket{\perp'} = \sum_{ij}c_{ij}\bra{\perp'}(C\ket{i})_{S} \otimes (\ket{p}\braket{p|j})_{C} = 0,
    \end{equation}
    with the last equality following from $\ket{\perp'} \in \mathcal{H}_{S} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}^{\perp}$ implying $\ket{j} \in \ket{p}_{C}^{\perp}$. Thus we find,
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} &=  |v_{3}|^{2}|\braket{B_{S}\otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)}, \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}}|^{2} \leq |\operatorname{Tr}(B^{*}_{S} \otimes P_{C}^{(\perp)} \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'})|^{2} \nonumber \\
                               &\leq |\sum_{ij}c_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}((B^{*}\ket{i})_{S} \otimes (P^{(\perp)}\ket{j})_{C}\bra{\perp'})|^{2} =  |\sum_{ij}c_{ij}\operatorname{Tr}((B^{*}\ket{i})_{S} \otimes \ket{j}_{C}\bra{\perp'})|^{2} = |\operatorname{Tr}(B^{*}_{S} \otimes \mathbb{I}_{C} \ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'})|^{2} \nonumber \\
                               & \leq |\operatorname{Tr}\left(B^{*} \operatorname{Tr}_{C}(\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'})\right)|^{2} = |\braket{B, \operatorname{Tr}_{C}(\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'})}|^{2}.
    \end{align}
    Since $\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}$ is a quantum state, $\operatorname{Tr}_{C}(\ket{\perp'}\bra{\perp'}) = \sigma$ is also a quantum state, thus
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} \leq \braket{B, B} \braket{\sigma, \sigma} \leq \braket{B, B} \leq \frac{1}{T-1}.
    \end{equation}
    where the final inequality follows from equation~\ref{eq:upperonB}. Combining the above equation with equation~\eqref{eq:cos} implies the statement.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lm:mattograph}
    Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix If
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $A = A^{\intercal}$
        \item for all $i \neq j$, matrix elements $[A]_{ij} \in \{-1, 0\}$
        \item $\sum_{j=1}^{n}[A]_{ij} = 0$ 
    \end{enumerate}
    then there exists a 
            
    graph $G$ over $n$ vertices such that the Laplacian for graph $G$ is matrix $A$.
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We first build the graph $G$ associated to matrix $A$, then show the Laplacian for graph $G$ is equal to $A$. 

    Let $V = [n]$ be a set of vertices and define the set of edges $E = \{\{i, j\} \in \binom{V}{2} \; | \; A_{ij} = -1 \}$. Consider the Laplacian associated to graph $G = (V, E)$ denoted $L_{G}$. Since $|V| = n$, $L_{G}$ is an $n \times n$ matrix. Let $i, j \in V$ with $i \neq j$. Since $L_{G}$ is a Laplacian, $[L_{G}]_{ij} \in \{-1, 0\}$. If $[L_{G}]_{ij} = -1$ then $\{i, j\} \in E$ implying $A_{ij} = -1$ therefore $[L_{G}]_{ij} = A_{ij}$. In the other case $[L_{G}]_{ij} = 0$ implying $\{i, j\} \notin E$ implying  $A_{ij} \neq -1$. Since $i \neq j$, we must have $A_{ij}=0$ implying $[L_{G}]_{ij} = A_{ij}$ as well. Thus for $i \neq j$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:offdiag}
        [L_{G}]_{ij} = A_{ij}.
    \end{equation}
    Let $i \in V$. Since $L_{G}$ is a Laplacian $\sum_{j=1}^{n}[L_{G}]_{ij} = 0$ thus we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \sum_{j=1}^{n}[L_{G}]_{ij} = \sum_{j=1}^{n}A_{ij} 
    \end{equation}
    which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        [L_{G}]_{ii} + \sum_{j\neq i}^{n} [L_{G}]_{ij} = A_{ii} + \sum_{j\neq i}^{n} A_{ij}.
    \end{equation}
    Using equation~\eqref{eq:offdiag}, we find 
    \begin{equation}
        [L_{G}]_{ii} + \sum_{j\neq i}^{n} A_{ij} = A_{ii} + \sum_{j\neq i}^{n} A_{ij}.
    \end{equation}
    which implies $[L_{G}]_{ii} = A_{ii}$. Thus for all $i, j \in V$
    \begin{equation}
        [L_{G}]_{ij} = A_{ij}
    \end{equation}
    implying the Laplacian for graph $G$ is the $n \times n$ matrix $A$.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma--2: body_md -->
Let $G$ be the graph defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} and $G_{m}$ be the subgraph associated to $V_{m} = \{(t,t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$, $G_{m}$ is a connected component of $G$.
<!-- end lemma--2 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
To show that $G_{m}$ is a component of $G$ it suffices to show that for all $v_{m} \in V_{m}$ and $v_{p} \in V \setminus V_{m}$ there does not exist an edge $\{v_{m}, v_{p}\} \in E$ where $E$ is the set of edges of $G$. If we let $L_{G}$ denote the Laplacian asssociated to $G$ then the previous statement is true if and only if $L_{G}$ block diagonalizes into $L_{G_{m}}$ and $L_{G_{p}}$ where $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ denote the subgraphs over vertices $V_{m}$ and $V \setminus V_{m}$ respectively. 

    Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} defines $L_{G}$ as $-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ expanded in the bases $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V}$ where $P_{v} = \ket{t_{A}}\bra{t_{B}}$ for $v = (t_{A}, t_{B})$. Thus $L_{G_{m}}$ and $L_{G_{p}}$ can be generated by expanding $-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ in the subsets $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V_{m}}$ and $\{P_{v}\}_{v\in V \setminus V_{m}}$. Defining $\Pi_{m}(\bullet) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}\bra{t} \bullet \ket{t}\bra{t}$ as the projection map into the subspace $\mathrm{span}\left(\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V_{m}}\right)$ we can define $L_{G_{m}}$ as $-4\mathcal{P}_{m}\circ\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\circ\mathcal{P}_{m}$ expanded in the basis $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V_{m}}$ and similarly $L_{G_{p}}$ as $-4(\mathcal{I} - \mathcal{P}_{m})\circ\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\circ(\mathcal{I} - \mathcal{P}_{m})$ expanded in the basis $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V \setminus V_{m}}$. The condition that $L_{G}$ block diagonalizes into $L_{G_{m}}$ and $L_{G_{p}}$ becomes equivalent to
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:condition}
        \Pi_{m} \circ (-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}) \circ (\mathcal{I} - \Pi_{m}) = 0,
    \end{equation}
    implying the off-diagonal blocks of $-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ expanded in the basis $\{P_{v}\}_{v\in V}$ vanish.

    Calculating $\Pi_{m} \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ we find,  
    \begin{align} 
        \Pi_{m} \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\bullet) &= \sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\left(\Pi_{m}(\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}) - \frac{1}{2}\Pi_{m}\left(\{\ket{-_{t}}\bra{-_{t}}, \bullet\}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                  &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\sum_{t'=0}^{T-1}\Big((\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1})^{2}\ket{t'}\bra{-_{t}}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t'} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1})\ket{t'}\bra{-_{t}} \bullet \ket{t'}\bra{t'} \nonumber \\
                                                  & \quad - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1})\ket{t'}\bra{t'}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t'}\Big) \nonumber \\ 
                                                  &= \frac{1}{2}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\ket{t}\bra{-_{t}}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{-_{t}}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t+1} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{t}\bra{-_{t}} \bullet \ket{t}\bra{t} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{t+1}\bra{-_{t}} \bullet \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}  \nonumber\\
                                                  & \quad - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{-_{t}}\bra{t+1}\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                  &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(-\ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t+1} - \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t+1} \nonumber \\ 
                                                  & \quad - \ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t} + \ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t+1} - \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\Big) \nonumber \\
                                                  &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{t=0}^{T-2}\Big(\ket{t}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t+1} \nonumber \\
                                                  &\quad - \ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t} - \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\Big).
\end{align}
    Now considering $\Pi_{m} \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \circ \Pi_{m}$ we find, 
    \begin{align}
        \Pi_{m} \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\circ\Pi_{m}(\bullet) &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Big(\ket{t}\bra{t+1}\Pi_{m}(\bullet)\ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{t}\Pi_{m}(\bullet)\ket{t}\bra{t+1} \nonumber \\
                                                              & \quad - \ket{t}\bra{t}\Pi_{m}(\bullet)\ket{t}\bra{t} - \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\Pi_{m}(\bullet)\ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\Big) \nonumber \\
    &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{t'=0}^{T}\Big(\ket{t}\braket{t+1|t'}\bra{t'}\bullet \ket{t'}\braket{t'|t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\braket{t|t'}\bra{t'}\bullet\ket{t'}\braket{t'|t}\bra{t+1} \nonumber \\
    &- \ket{t}\braket{t|t'}\bra{t'}\bullet\ket{t'}\braket{t'|t}\bra{t} - \ket{t+1}\braket{t+1|t'}\bra{t'}\bullet\ket{t'}\braket{t'|t+1}\bra{t+1}\Big) \nonumber \\
    &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Big(\ket{t}\bra{t+1}\bullet \ket{t+1}\bra{t} + \ket{t+1}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t+1} \nonumber \\
    & \quad - \ket{t}\bra{t}\bullet\ket{t}\bra{t} - \ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\bullet\ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}\Big) = \Pi \circ \tilde{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\bullet).
    \end{align}
    Therefore $\Pi_{m} \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} \circ (\mathcal{I} - \Pi_{m}) = 0$ implying equation~\eqref{eq:condition}, thus $L_{G}$ block diagonalizes into $L_{G_{m}}$ and $L_{G_{p}}$ implying both $G_{m}$ and $G_{p}$ are components of graph $G$.

    To show $G_{m}$ is connected, we consider a family of subgraphs $\{G_{m}^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^{T-1}$ where subgraph $G_{m}^{(t)}$ contains the set of vertices $\{(t',t')\}_{t'=0}^{t} \subseteq V_{m}$. Note, by definition $G_{m}^{T-1} = G_{m}$. To show $G_{m}$ is connected we proceed by induction. Consider the base case of $G_{m}^{(1)}$ containing vertices $\{(0,0), (1,1)\}$. $G_{m}^{(1)}$ is connected if there exists an edge connecting $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$. For vertices $(0, 0)$ and $(1, 1)$ we find,
    \begin{equation}
        [L_{G}]_{(0,0), (1,1)} = -4\braket{P_{(0,0)}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{(1,1)})}_{HS} = \braket{\ket{0}\bra{0}, - \ket{0}\bra{0} -\ket{2}\bra{2} + 2 \ket{1}\bra{1} }_{HS} = -1.
    \end{equation} 
    Thus there exists an edge connecting vertices $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$ implying $G_{m}^{(1)}$ is connected. Assume induction hypothesis: $G_{m}^{(t)}$ is connected for all $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-1\}$, and consider subgraph $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$. By definition $G_{m}^{(t)}$ is a subgraph of $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$ with $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$ containing all the vertices of $G_{m}^{(t)}$ along with vertex $(t+1,t+1)$. Thus assuming our induction hypothesis, $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$ is connected if there exists a vertex in $G_{m}^{(t)}$ with an edge in $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$ connecting it to vertex $(t+1,t+1)$.  To show this consider vertices $(t, t)$, associated to subgraph $G_{m}^{(t)}$, and $(t+1, t+1)$, associated to $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$, we find 
    \begin{equation}
        [L_{G}]_{(t,t), (t+1,t+1)} = -4\braket{P_{(t,t)}, \circ \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(P_{(t+1,t+1)})} = \braket{\ket{t}\bra{t}, -\ket{t}\bra{t} - \ket{t+2}\bra{t+2} + 2\ket{t+1}\bra{t+1}} = -1.
    \end{equation}
    Thus there exists an edge connecting vertices $(t, t)$ to $(t+1, t+1)$ implying $G_{m}^{(t+1)}$ is connected. Therefore for all $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-1\}$ the subgraphs $G_{m}^{(t)}$ are connected implying $G_{m}^{(T-1)} = G_{m}$ is connected as well.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lm:GA}
    For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, the subgraph $G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected.
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, let $G_{A}^{(t)}$ denote the subgraph associated to the set of vertices $((t-1, t-1), (T-1, t-1)]$. Consider the family of subgraphs $\{[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}\}_{i=t}^{T-1}$ where $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$ denotes the subgraph of $G_{A}^{(t)}$ associated to vertices $((t-1, t-1), (i, t-1)]$. Note, by definition $G_{A}^{(t)} = [G_{A}^{(t)}]_{T-1}$. To prove $G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected we proceed by induction. Consider the base case of $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{t}$ associated to vertices $((t-1, t-1), (t, t-1)] = \{(t, t-1)\}$. By definition of a singleton graph $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{t}$ is a connected. Assume induction hypothesis: $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$ is connected for all $i \in \{t, t+1,\cdots, T-1\}$, and consider subgraph $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$. By definition $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$ is a subgraph of $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ containing all the vertices associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$ in addition to $(i+1, t-1)$. Assuming our induction hypothesis, $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ is connected if there exists a vertex associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$ with an edge associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ connecting it to vertex $(i+1, t-1)$. To show this consider vertices $(i, t-1)$, associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$, and $(i+1, t-1)$, associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i}$, we find 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:GA}
        \left[L_{[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}}\right]_{(i, t-1), (i+1, t-1)} &= -4\braket{\ket{i}\bra{t-1}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{i+1}\bra{t-1})} = \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\braket{i|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|i+1}\left(2 - 4|\braket{t-1|-_{t'}}|^{2}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                  &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left((\delta_{i,t'} - \delta_{i, t'+1})(\delta_{t', i+1} - \delta_{t'+1,i+1} )\left(1- |\delta_{t-1,t'} - \delta_{t-1,t'+1}|^{2}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                  &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left((\delta_{i,t'}\delta_{t',i+1} - \delta_{i,t'}\delta_{t'+1,i+1} - \delta_{i, t'+1}\delta_{t',i+1} + \delta_{i, t'+1}\delta_{t'+1,i+1}) \left(1- \delta_{t-1,t'} - \delta_{t-1,t'+1}\right)\right) \nonumber  \\
                                                                  &= -1 + \delta_{t-1,i} + \delta_{t-1, i+1} = -1,
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from $i \geq t$. From the definition of the Laplacian for $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$, equation~\eqref{eq:GA} implies there exists an edge associated to $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ connecting vertex $(i, t-1)$ to $(i+1,t-1)$ implying $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ is connected. Therefore for all $i \in \{t, t+1, \cdots, T-1\}$ the subgraph $[G_{A}^{(i)}]_{i}$ is connected. Therefore for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, the subgraph $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{T-1} = G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected, and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:GA} holds.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lm:GB}
    For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, the subgraph $G_{B}^{(t)}$ is connected.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, let $G_{B}^{(t)}$ denote the subgraph associated to the set of vertices $[(0, t), (t,t))$. Consider the family of subgraphs $\{[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}\}_{i=1}^{t}$ where $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$ denotes the subgraph of $G_{B}^{(t)}$ associated to vertices $[(0, t), (i,t))$. Note, by definition $G_{B}^{(t)} = [G_{B}^{(t)}]_{t}$. To prove $G_{B}^{(t)}$ is connected we proceed by induction. Consider the base case of $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{1}$ associated to vertices $[(0, t), (1, t)) = \{(0, t)\}$. By definition of a singleton graph $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{0}$ is connected. Assume induction hypothesis: $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$ is connected for all $i \in \{1,\cdots, t-1\}$, and consider subgraph $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$. By definition $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$ is a subgraph of $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ containing all the vertices associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$ in addition to $(i, t)$. Assuming our induction hypothesis, $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ is connected if there exists a vertex associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$ with an edge associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ connecting it to vertex $(i, t)$. To show this consider vertices $(i-1, t)$, associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i}$, and $(i, t)$, associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$, we find 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:GB}
        \left[L_{[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}}\right]_{(i-1, t), (i, t)} &= -4\braket{\ket{i-1}\bra{t}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{i}\bra{t})} = \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\braket{i-1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|i}\left(2 - 4|\braket{t|-_{t'}}|^{2}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                  &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left((\delta_{i-1,t'} - \delta_{i-1, t'+1})(\delta_{t', i} - \delta_{t'+1,i} )\left(1- |\delta_{t,t'} - \delta_{t,t'+1}|^{2}\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                  &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left((\delta_{i-1,t'}\delta_{t',i} - \delta_{i-1,t'}\delta_{t'+1,i} - \delta_{i-1, t'+1}\delta_{t',i} + \delta_{i-1, t'+1}\delta_{t'+1,i}) \left(1- \delta_{t,t'} - \delta_{t,t'+1}\right)\right) \nonumber  \\
                                                                  &= -1 + \delta_{t,i-1} + \delta_{t, i} = -1,
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from $i \leq t-1$. From the definition of the Laplacian for $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$, equation~\eqref{eq:GB} implies there exists an edge associated to $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ connecting vertex $(i, t)$ to $(i+1,t)$ implying $[G_{A}^{(t)}]_{i+1}$ is connected. Therefore for all $i \in \{1, 2, \cdots, t\}$ the subgraph $[G_{B}^{(i)}]_{i}$ is connected. Therefore for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, the subgraph $[G_{B}^{(t)}]_{T-1} = G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected, and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:GB} holds.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lm:subgraph}
    For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, the subgraph $G_{p}^{(t)}$ is connected.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
For all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, let $G_{p}^{(t)}$ be the subgraph of $G_{p}$ associated to the vertices $\left((t-1,t-1), (t, t)\right)$. We can partition the vertices into subsets $((t-1, t-1), (T-1, t-1)]$ and $[(T-1, t-1), (t-1, t-1))$ and define subgraphs $G_{A}^{(t)}$ and $G_{B}^{(t)}$ respectively. Let $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ be vertices associated to graph $G_{p}^{(t)}$. By definition of $G_{A}^{(t)}$ and $G_{B}^{(t)}$, vertices $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ must be associated to either $G_{A}^{(t)}$ or $G_{B}^{(t)}$. 

    Assume the case when $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ are associated to the same graph. Consider the sub-case when this graph is $G_{A}^{(t)}$. Since Lemma~\ref{lm:GA} implies $G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{A}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$. Similarly consider the sub-case when this graph is $G_{B}^{(t)}$. Lemma~\ref{lm:GB} implies $G_{B}^{(t)}$ is connected, thus there exists a walk in $G_{B}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$. Therefore in both sub-cases there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$.

    Now assume the case when $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ are associated to different graphs. Without loss of generality take $v_{1}$ as associated to $G_{A}^{(t)}$ and $v_{2}$ as associated to $G_{B}^{(t)}$. Assume for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$ there exists an edge in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting a vertex $v_{A}$ associated to subgraph $G_{A}$ to a vertex $v_{B}$ associated to subgraph $G_{B}^{(t)}$.  Since Lemma~\ref{lm:GA} implies $G_{A}^{(t)}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{A}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{A}$. Using our assumption, there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{B}$. Since Lemma~\ref{lm:GB} implies $G_{B}^{(t)}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{B}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{B}$ to $v_{2}$. Thus there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$. Therefore it suffices to show our assumption in-order to prove there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$.

    To prove our assumption consider vertices $v_{A} = (t-1, t)$ and $v_{B} = (t, t-1)$ associated to $G_{A}^{(t)}$ and $G_{B}^{(t)}$ respectively. From Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph}, the Laplacian for subgraph $G_{p}^{(t)}$, denoted $L_{G_{p}^{(t)}}$, is $-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ expanded in the basis $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in ((t-1, t-1), (t,t))}$ for $P:V\mapsto \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H})$ defined by $(t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V \mapsto P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})} = \ket{t_{A}}\bra{t_{B}}$. Thus we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:GPT}
        \left[L_{G_{p}^{(t)}}\right]_{v_{A}, v_{B}} &=  -4 \braket{\ket{t-1}\bra{t}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}(\ket{t}\bra{t-1})} = -4\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\braket{t-1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t}\braket{t-1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t} \\
&= -\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}(\delta_{t',t-1} - \delta_{t'+1,t-1})^{2}(\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t'+1,t})^{2} = -\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}(\delta_{t',t-1} + \delta_{t'+1,t-1})(\delta_{t',t} + \delta_{t'+1,t}) \\
&= -\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}(\delta_{t', t-1}\delta_{t',t} + \delta_{t',t-1}\delta_{t'+1,t} + \delta_{t'+1, t-1}\delta_{t',t} + \delta_{t'+1,t-1} \delta_{t'+1, t}) = -1.
    \end{align}
    From the definition of the Laplacian for $G_{p}^{(t)}$, equation~\eqref{eq:GPT} implies there exists an edge associated to $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting $v_{A}$ to $v_{B}$. Thus for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, there exists an edge associated to $G_{p}^{(t)}$ connecting a vertex $v_{A}$, associated to $G_{A}^{(t)}$, to a vertex $v_{B}$, associated to $G_{B}^{(t)}$.

    Since in both cases there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t)}$ that connects vertex $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$, $G_{p}^{(t)}$ is connected by definition, and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:subgraph} follows.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma--3: body_md -->
Let $G$ be the graph defined in Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph} and $G_{p}$ be the subgraph associated to $V_{p} = V \setminus \{(t, t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$, $G_{p}$ is a connected component of $G$.
<!-- end lemma--3 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Since Lemma~\ref{lm:mixcomp} states that the subgraph $G_{m}$ associated to the set vertices $V_{m} = \{(t, t)\}_{t=0}^{T-1}$ is a component of $G$, then the subgraph associated to the set of vertices of $V \setminus V_{m}$ must also be a component of $G$. Therefore $G_{p}$ is a component of $G$.

    To show $G_{p}$ is connected consider the family of subgraphs of $G_{p}$, $\{G_{p}^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^{T-1}$ where each subgraph $G_{p}^{(t)}$ is associated to vertices $((t-1,t-1), (t, t))$. Let $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ be two vertices associated to graph $G_{p}$. By the definition of subgraphs $\{G_{p}^{(t)}\}_{t=1}^{T-1}$ there exists $t_{1}, t_{2} \in \{1, 2, \cdots T-1\}$ such that $v_{1}$ is associated to subgraph $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ and $v_{2}$ is associated to subgraph $G_{p}^{(t_{2})}$. Assume for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$ there exists an edge associated to graph $G_{p}$ connecting a vertex $v_{ex}^{(t)}$ associated to $G_{p}^{(t)}$ to a vertex $v_{en}^{(t+1)}$ associated to $G_{p}^{(t+1)}$. If $t_{1} = t_{2}$, vertices $v_{1}$ and $v_{2}$ are associated to graph $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$. Since Lemma~\ref{lm:subgraph} implies $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$. If $t_{1} \neq t_{2}$, without loss of generality we can assume $t_{2} > t_{1}$, then vertex $v_{1}$ is associated to $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ and vertex $v_{2}$ is associated to $G_{p}^{(t_{2})}$ with $G_{p}^{(t_{1})} \neq G_{p}^{(t_{2})}$. By our assumption, there exists an edge connecting $v_{ex}^{(t_{1})}$ to $v_{en}^{(t_{1}+1)}$, and by using the connectedness of $G_{p}^{(t_{1}+1)}$ implied by Lemma~\ref{lm:subgraph} there exists walk in $G_{p}^{(t_{1}+1)}$ connecting $v_{en}^{(t_{1}+1)}$ to $v_{ex}^{(t_{1}+1)}$, therefore there exists a walk in $G$ connecting $v_{ex}^{(t_{1})}$ to $v_{ex}^{(t_{1}+1)}$. Applying this result $t_{2} - t_{1}$ times gives us a walk $G$ connecting $v_{ex}^{(t_{1})}$ to $v_{ex}^{(t_{2})}$. Since Lemma~\ref{lm:subgraph} implies $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t_{1})}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{ex}^{(t_{1})}$, therefore there exists a walk in $G_{p}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{ex}^{(t_{2})}$. Similarly, since Lemma~\ref{lm:subgraph} implies $G_{p}^{(t_{2})}$ is connected, there exists a walk in $G_{p}^{(t_{2})}$ connecting $v_{ex}^{(t_{2})}$ to $v_{2}$, therefore there exists a walk in $G_{p}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$. Since in all cases, for $v_{1}, v_{2} \in V$ there exists a walk in $G_{p}$ connecting $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$, $G_{p}$ is connected. Thus it suffices to show our assumption; for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$  there exists an edge associated to graph $G_{p}$ connecting a vertex $v_{ex}^{(t)}$ associated to $G_{p}^{(t)}$ to a vertex $v_{en}^{(t+1)}$ associated $G_{p}^{(t+1)}$, in-order to show graph $G_{p}$ is connected.

    To prove our assumption, let $t  \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$ and consider vertices $v_{ex}^{(t)} = (0, t)$ and $v_{en}^{(t+1)} = (0,t+1)$ associated to graph $G_{p}$. From the definitions of $G_{p}^{(t)}$ and $G_{p}^{(t+1)}$, vertex $v_{ex}^{(t)}$ is associated to graph $G_{p}^{(t)}$ and vertex $v_{en}^{(t+1)}$ is associated to $G_{p}^{(t+1)}$.  From Lemma~\ref{lm:rotadistograph}, the Laplacian for subgraph $G_{p}$, denoted $L_{G_{p}}$, is $-4\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ expanded in the basis $\{P_{v}\}_{v \in V_{p}}$  for $P: V \mapsto \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})$ defined by $(t_{A}, t_{B}) \in V \mapsto P_{(t_{A}, t_{B})} = \ket{t_{A}}\bra{t_{B}}$. Thus we find, 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:edget}
        \left[L_{G_{p}}\right]_{v_{ex}^{(t)}, v_{en}^{(t+1)}} &= -4\braket{\ket{0}\bra{t}, \tilde{\mathcal{D}}_{prop}(\ket{0}\bra{t+1})} = -4\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(|\braket{-_{t'}|0}|^{2}\braket{t+1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t} - \frac{1}{2}\braket{t+1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                              &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\left(2 - 4|\braket{-_{t'}|0}|^{2}\right)\braket{t+1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t} \right) = 2\sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\left(1 - |\delta_{t',0} - \delta_{t'+1,0}|^{2}\right)\braket{t+1|-_{t'}}\braket{-_{t'}|t}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                              &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\left(1 - \delta_{t',0} + \delta_{t'+1,0}\right)(\delta_{t',t+1} - \delta_{t'+1,t+1})(\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t'+1,t})\right) \nonumber \\
                                                              &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}\left(\left(1 - \delta_{t',0} + \delta_{t'+1,0}\right)(\delta_{t',t+1}\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1}\delta_{t'+1,t} - \delta_{t'+1,t+1}\delta_{t',t} + \delta_{t'+1,t+1}\delta_{t'+1,t})\right) \nonumber \\
                                                              &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-2}(\delta_{t',t+1}\delta_{t',t} - \delta_{t',t+1}\delta_{t'+1,t} - \delta_{t'+1,t+1}\delta_{t',t} + \delta_{t'+1,t+1}\delta_{t'+1,t}) = -1
\end{align}
where the 2\textsuperscript{nd} to last equality follows from $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$. From the definition of Laplacian $L_{G_{p}}$, equation~\eqref{eq:edget} implies there exists an edge associated to $G_{p}$ connecting $v_{ex}^{(t)}$ to $v_{en}^{(t+1)}$. Thus for all $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, T-1\}$, there exists an edge associated to graph $G_{p}$ connecting a vertex $v_{p}^{(t)}$ associated to $G_{p}^{(t)}$ to a vertex $v_{en}^{(t+1)}$ associated to $G_{p}^{(t+1)}$, implying $G_{p}$ is connected. The statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:purecomp} thus follows.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma--4: body_md -->
Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$ and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} using $V$ as well as $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ according to equation~\ref{eq:Dinp} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}} = \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{M}) \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C})].
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $\operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ the circuit rotation associated to $V$, is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}
<!-- end lemma--4 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Defining the rotated version of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ as $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}^{(V)} = \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}} \circ \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}$ we find     
    \begin{equation}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}^{(V)}|_{\mathcal{U}^{(V)\dagger}[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})]} } = \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)\dagger}[\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}})}}].
    \end{equation}
    From Lemma~\ref{lm:onlyhist} we can simplify the above equation as
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Dinpkern}
