        \ket{x_{>t+2}}\bra{x_{>t+2}}\otimes [P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}]_{t+2,t+1,t} \otimes \ket{x_{<t}}\bra{x_{<t}} = \sum_{s \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}} \ket{x_{>t+2}sx_{<t}}\bra{x_{>t+2}sx_{<t}} \in \mathbb{D}
    \end{align}
    it follows that
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})}(A) \in \mathbb{D}
    \end{equation}
    implying $\mathbb{D}$ is an invariant subspace. Since for all $A \in \mathbb{D}$ and $B \in \mathbb{O}$ we have $\braket{A, B} = \sum_{x} \sum_{y\neq z}a_{x}b_{y,z}\braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \ket{y}\bra{z}} = 0$, we have $\mathbb{O} = \mathbb{D}^{\perp}$. Therefore we find $\mathbb{O}$ is also an invariant subspace of $\mathcal{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})}$, since $\mathcal{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})}$ is Hermitian with respect to the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. Thus we have
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:partitionbreakup1}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})} = \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}} \oplus \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}.
    \end{equation}

    Consider $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ restricted to $\mathbb{D} = \mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}} \oplus \mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ Since for all $A \in \mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ and $B \in \mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}$ we find $\braket{A, B} = \sum_{x\in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}}\sum_{y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}}a_{x}b_{y}\braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \ket{y}\bra{y}} = 0$, we have that $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}} = \mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{\perp_{\mathbb{D}}}$. Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} implies $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}} \subseteq \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}}$ therefore $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}$ is an invariant subspace of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}$. Similarly, since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}$ is Hermitian with respect to the Hibert-Schmidt inner product on $\mathbb{D}$, $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}$ is an invariant subspace of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}$, and $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ is the orthogonal complement of $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}$ with respect to $\mathbb{D}$, we find that $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ must also be an invariant subspace of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}$. Therefore 
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}} = \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}} \oplus \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}}.
    \end{equation}
    The above equation combined with~\eqref{eq:partitionbreakup1} implies the statement of this lemma.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lm:Oblocks}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define the subspaces $\mathbb{O}$ and $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ according to equations~\eqref{eq:subspacedefs} and~\eqref{eq:diffO} respectively, then
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}} = \bigoplus_{d\neq 0^{T}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Fix $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots T-3\}$ and $d \in \{0,1\}^{T}$ such that $d \neq 0^{T}$. Calculating,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:casesford}
        &\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d}) = \ket{x_{>t+2}}\bra{[x \oplus d]_{>t+2}} \otimes \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d}_{t+2,t+1,t}) \otimes \ket{x_{<t}}\bra{[x\oplus d]_{<t}} \nonumber \\
        &= \begin{cases}
            0 \text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t},\; x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}} \\
            -\frac{1}{2}\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d} \text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}},\; x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t}  \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}} \\
            -\frac{1}{2}\ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d} \text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}},\; x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t}  \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}} \\
            - \ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d} \text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}, \; x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}, x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \neq x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \\
            B - \ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d}\text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t},\; x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}, x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \neq x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t}
        \end{cases}
    \end{align}
    where we have defined 
    \begin{equation}
        B = \frac{1}{4}\ket{x_{>t+2}}\bra{[x \oplus d]_{>t+2}} \otimes [P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}]_{t+2,t+1,t} \otimes \ket{x_{<t}}\bra{[x\oplus d]_{<t}}.
    \end{equation}
    Note $B \in \mathbb{O}_{d}$, therefore equation~\eqref{eq:casesford} implies $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d}) \in \mathbb{O}_{d}$ for all $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$. Thus we find 
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d}) = \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d}) = \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d}) \in \mathbb{O}_{d}
    \end{align}
    implying for all $A \in \mathbb{O}_{d}$ we have $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}(A) \in \mathbb{O}_{d}$. This statement holds for all $d \neq 0^{T}$ therefore the subspaces $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ are invariant under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}$ implying the statement of the lemma.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lm:helperlemma}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define the subspace $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ for $d\neq 0^{T}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:diffO}. Let 
    \begin{equation}
        A = \sum_{x} a_{x} \ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d} \in \mathbb{O}_{d}
    \end{equation}
    then 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} &\leq -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2} -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{x}|^{2}. 
    \end{align}
    where
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:edges}
        \mathrm{S}_{E} = \left\{\{x,y\} \in \binom{\{0,1\}^{T}}{2} \; \Big| \; \exists t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}, \substack{d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} = 000, \\ x_{>t+2} = y_{>t+2}, \\  x_{<t} = y_{<t}, \\ \{x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t},y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}\} \in E}  \right\} 
    \end{equation}
    with $E = \left\{\{010, 100\}, \{110, 101\}\right\}$ and 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:boundary}
        \mathrm{S}_{B} = \left\{x \in \{0, 1\}^{T} \; \Big| \; \exists t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}, \substack{d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 000, \\ x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}} \,\mathrm{ or }\\ x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}\right\}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Calculating $\braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})}$ gives us two cases, either $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} = 0$ or $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 0$.
                  
                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                               
                
    Consider the case of $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} = 000$, for $x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}, y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})} &= \delta_{y_{>t+2}, x_{>t+2}}\delta_{y_{<t}, x_{<t}}\left(\frac{1}{4}- \delta_{y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}, x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}}\right).
    \end{align}
    For $x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}, y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t} \notin \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})} = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Consider the case of $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 000$   we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})} &= -\frac{\delta_{x,y}}{2}\left(\mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}] + \mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}]\right)
    \end{align}
    where $\mathbf{1}$ denotes the indicator function.

    Now consider calculating $\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)}$ for the case of $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} = 000$, we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)} &= \sum_{x,y} a_{y}^{*}a_{x}\braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})} \nonumber \\
        &= \sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y},s_{x} \in \{0,1\}^{3}}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}\braket{\ket{s_{y}}\bra{s_{y}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{s_{x}}\bra{s_{x}})} \nonumber \\
        &= \sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y},s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}\left(\frac{1}{4} - \delta_{s_{x}, s_{y}}\right) \nonumber \\
        &= \frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\left(\sum_{s_{y},s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} - 4\sum_{s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}|^{2} \right) \nonumber \\
        &= -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\left(3\sum_{s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}|^{2} - \sum_{s_{y},s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} \neq s_{y}}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} \right).
    \end{align}
    Order $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ according to $010 < 100 < 101 < 110$ allows us to simplify the above expression as
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)} &= -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\left(3\sum_{s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}|^{2} - \sum_{s_{y},s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} < s_{y}}2 \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}} (a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}) \right) \nonumber \\
        &= -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y}, s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} < s_{y}}\left(|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}|^{2} + |a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}|^{2} - 2 \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}} (a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}^{*}a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}}) \right) \nonumber \\
        &= -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y}, s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} < s_{y}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} - a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}|^{2}.
    \end{align}
    Now consider calculating $\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)}$ for the case of $d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 000$, we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)} &= \sum_{x,y} a_{y}^{*}a_{x}\braket{\ket{y}\bra{y\oplus d}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{x}\bra{x\oplus d})} \nonumber \\
        &= -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x}|a_{x}|^{2}\left(\mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}] + \mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}]\right).
    \end{align}

    To calculate $\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)}$ we first define sets of indices
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{cases}
            \mathcal{T}^{0} = \{t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\} \; | \; d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} = 000\} \\
            \mathcal{T}^{\neq} = \{t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\} \; | \; d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 000\}
        \end{cases}.
    \end{equation}
    We find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} &= \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)} = \sum_{t\in \mathcal{T}^{0}}\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)} + \sum_{t\in \mathcal{T}^{\neq}}\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(A)}
    \end{align}
    which becomes 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} = -&\frac{1}{4}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{0}}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y}, s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} < s_{y}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} - a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}|^{2} \nonumber \\
        &-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}^{\neq}}\sum_{x}|a_{x}|^{2}\left(\mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}] + \mathbf{1}[x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \oplus d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}]\right).
    \end{align}
    Using our definition of $\mathrm{S}_{B}$ and fixing $x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}$ the second term in the above equation contributes at most $- |a_{x}|^{2} / 2$. Therefore we can write
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} &\leq -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{0}}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{s_{y}, s_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}; s_{x} < s_{y}}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} - a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}|^{2} -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{x}|^{2} \nonumber \\
        &\leq -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}^{0}}\sum_{x_{>t+2}}\sum_{x_{<t}}\sum_{\{s_{x},s_{y}\} \in E}|a_{x_{>t+2}s_{x}x_{<t}} - a_{x_{>t+2}s_{y}x_{<t}}|^{2} -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{x}|^{2}
    \end{align}
    where we have used our definition of $E$. Similarly, using our definition of $\mathrm{S}_{E}$ and fixing a pair $\{x, y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}$ the first term in the above equation contributes at most $- |a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2} / 4$. Thus we conclude,
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} &\leq -\frac{1}{4}\sum_{\{x,y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2} -\frac{1}{2}\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{x}|^{2}. 
    \end{align}
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lm:diffOgap}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define the subspace $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ for $d \neq 0^{T}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:diffO}, then 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}\right) \geq 1 / 4T^{3}
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Our strategy is to bound the Rayleigh quotient. From Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} and our definition of $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}} &=  \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})}} \cap \mathbb{O}_{d} = \left(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}) \oplus P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\right) \cap \mathbb{O}_{d} = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}) \cap \mathbb{O}_{d} \nonumber \\
        &= \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d} \; | \;  x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)} \text{ and }  x \oplus d \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)} \}\right).
    \end{align}
    which implies
    \begin{align}
        \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}}^{\perp_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}} &= \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d} \; | \;  x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)} \text{ or }  x \oplus d \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)} \}\right) = \mathrm{span}\left(\{\ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d} \; | \; x \in \mathrm{S}_{O} \}\right)
    \end{align}
    where we have defined 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{S}_{O} = \{x \in \{0,1\}^{T} \; | \; x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)} \text{ or } x \oplus d \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\}
    \end{equation}
    Let $A \in\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}}^{\perp_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}}$ expanding in the computational basis
    \begin{equation}
        A = \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}} a_{x} \ket{x}\bra{x \oplus d}.
    \end{equation}
     Define $\mathrm{S}_{E}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{B}$ according to equations~\eqref{eq:edges} and~\eqref{eq:boundary} of Lemma~\ref{lm:helperlemma} respectively. Note, $\mathrm{S}_{B} \subseteq \mathrm{S}_{O}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{E} \subseteq \binom{\mathrm{S}_{O}}{2}$. Consider the graph $G = (\mathrm{S}_{O}, \mathrm{S}_{E})$. For each vertex $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ we can construct a path from $x$ to a boundary vertex $b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}$ as follows. If $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ and $x \in \mathrm{S}_{B}$ then our path is simply $\{\}$. Thus we take $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ and $x \notin \mathrm{S}_{B}$ which implies there exists an index $s \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ such that $d_{s+2}d_{s+1}d_{s} = 000$ and $x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$. Define the set $F(d) = \{t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\} \; | \; d_{t+2}d_{t+1}d_{t} \neq 000\}$. Since $d \neq 0^{T}$ we know that $F(d) \neq \emptyset$. Take the index $f = \arg\min_{f \in F(d)}|f - s|$, if $f - s > 0$ then we define our path according to the sequence of vertices
     \begin{equation}
         \label{eq:path1}
         x = x_{>s+2}x_{s+2}10x_{<s} \rightarrow x_{>s+2}10x_{s+2}x_{<s} \rightarrow \cdots  \rightarrow x_{> f}10x_{\geq s+2}^{\leq f}x_{<s} \rightarrow x_{> f+1}10x_{\geq s+2}^{\leq f+1}x_{<s} \in \mathrm{S}_{B}
     \end{equation}
     if $f - s < 0$ then we define our path according to the sequence of vertices 
     \begin{equation}
         \label{eq:path2}
         x = x_{>s+2}10x_{s}x_{<s} \rightarrow x_{>s+2}x_{s}10x_{<s} \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow  x_{>s+2}x_{\geq s}^{\leq f - 1}10x_{<f+1} \rightarrow x_{>s+2}x_{\geq s}^{\leq f }10x_{<f} \in \mathrm{S}_{B},
     \end{equation}
     where we have removed cycles to ensure the resulting sequence of edges are valid paths. By construction each pair of vertices is an edge in $\mathrm{S}_{E}$ since $f$ is the index of the closest 3-bit window to $s$ that is not zero.  

     Let $\gamma_{x}$ be the path associated to $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ defined according to equations~\eqref{eq:path1} and~\eqref{eq:path2} along with $b_{x} \in \mathrm{S}_{B}$ being the vertex in $\mathrm{S}_{B}$ that $\gamma_{x}$ connects $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ to. Define $x_{i}$ to be the $i$-th vertex occurring in the path $\gamma_{x}$, implying $x_{|\gamma_{x}|} = b_{x}$ and $x_{0} = x$, for all $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ we can write
     \begin{equation}
         a_{x} = a_{b_{x}} + \sum_{i=0}^{|\gamma_{x}|-1}(a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}).
     \end{equation}
     From Cauchy-Schwarz we find
     \begin{equation}
         |a_{x}|^{2} \leq (|\gamma_{x}| + 1)\left(|a_{b_{x}}|^{2} + \sum_{i=0}^{|\gamma_{x}|-1}|a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}
     From our definition of $\gamma_{x}$, the length of the path is upper-bounded by $|f - s|$. Since both $f, s \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ we have $|\gamma_{x}| \leq T- 3$ implying
     \begin{equation}
         |a_{x}|^{2} \leq T\left(|a_{b_{x}}|^{2} + \sum_{i=0}^{|\gamma_{x}|-1}|a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}|^{2}\right) = T \left(|a_{b_{x}}|^{2} + \sum_{\{x_{i}, x_{i+1}\} \in \gamma_{x}}|a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}
     Summing over $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ we find
     \begin{equation}
         \sum_{x\in \mathrm{S}_{O}}|a_{x}|^{2} = \braket{A, A} \leq T \left(\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}}|a_{b_{x}}|^{2} + \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}}\sum_{\{x_{i}, x_{i+1}\} \in \gamma_{x}}|a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}
     Defining $N_{b} = \{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O} \; | \; b = b_{x}\}$ we can write
     \begin{equation}
         \braket{A, A} \leq T \left(\sum_{b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|N_{b}||a_{b}|^{2} + \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}}\sum_{\{x_{i}, x_{i+1}\} \in \gamma_{x}}|a_{x_{i}} - a_{x_{i+1}}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}
     Similarly, defining $N_{e} = \{x \in \mathrm{S}_{O} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x} \}$ we can write
     \begin{equation}
         \braket{A, A} \leq T \left(\sum_{b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|N_{b}||a_{b}|^{2} + \sum_{\{x, y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|N_{\{x,y\}}||a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}

     Consider $N_{b}$, fix indices $f, s \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ as used in the construction of our paths $\gamma_{x}$. For each pair $f$ and $s$ we can reverse the sequence of vertices given in equation~\eqref{eq:path1} or equation~\eqref{eq:path2} to arrive at a unique $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$. Since there are $T-2$ choices for both $f$ and $s$ we have $|N_{b}| \leq  T^{2}$ for all $b \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ therefore we find 
     \begin{equation}
         \braket{A, A} \leq T \left(2T^{2}\sum_{b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{b}|^{2} + \sum_{\{x, y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|N_{\{x,y\}}||a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}
    
    Consider $N_{e}$, for $e \notin \gamma_{x}$ for all $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$ we have $|N_{e}| = 0$. For the case of $e \in \gamma_{x}$ for some $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$, if we fix $f, s \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$, then we can reverse the sequence of vertices in either equation~\eqref{eq:path1} or equation~\eqref{eq:path2} starting at $e$ until we reach index $s$ arriving at a unique $x \in \mathrm{S}_{O}$. Since there are $T-2$ choices for both $s$ and $f$ we find $|N_{e}|\leq T^{2}$ implying 
     \begin{equation}
         \label{eq:fin}
         \braket{A, A} \leq T \left(2T^{2}\sum_{b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{b}|^{2} + T^{2}\sum_{\{x, y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2}\right).
     \end{equation}

     From Lemma~\ref{lm:helperlemma} which holds for all $A \in \mathbb{O}_{d}$ we find 
     \begin{align}
         -\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)} \geq  \frac{1}{4}\left(2\sum_{b \in \mathrm{S}_{B}}|a_{b}|^{2} + \sum_{\{x, y\} \in \mathrm{S}_{E}}|a_{x} - a_{y}|^{2}\right) \geq \frac{1}{4T^{3}}\braket{A,A}.
     \end{align}
     Therefore we have 
     \begin{equation}
         \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}\right) = \inf_{\substack{A \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}}^{\perp_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}} \\ \braket{A, A} \neq 0}}\left(-\frac{\braket{A, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}(A)}}{\braket{A,A}}\right) \geq  \frac{1}{4T^{3}}
     \end{equation}
     as stated.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lm:DunaryO}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define the subspace $\mathbb{O}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:subspacedefs}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}\right) \geq 1 / 4 T^{3}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Define $\mathbb{O}_{d}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:diffO}. From Lemma~\ref{lm:Oblocks} we find
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}\right) \geq \inf_{d \neq 0^{T}}\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}_{d}}\right).
    \end{equation}
    From Lemma~\ref{lm:diffOgap} we conclude
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}\right)\geq \frac{1}{4T^{3}}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lm:blockismarkovchain}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define subspace  $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:subspacedefs}. Let $Q$ be the matrix formed by elements
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Q}
        Q_{x,y} = \braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}(\ket{y}\bra{y})} \text{ for } x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)},
    \end{equation}
    then $Q$ is a transition-rate matrix for a continuous-time Markov chain over the state space $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ with a reversible and irreducible jump chain given by equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain} with steady-state
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:steadystate}
        \pi = \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}} \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|} \hat{x}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
By construction the matrix elements of $Q$ form an $|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}| \times |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|$ matrix, therefore it suffices to show the conditions of equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef} to prove $Q$ is a transition-rate matrix associated to a continuous-time Markov chain over the state space $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$.
    
    Consider the first of the conditions given in equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef}. Since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}$ is Hermitian with respect to the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product on $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ and is a valid Lindbladian dissipator we have $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}} \preceq 0$ implying $Q_{x,x} \leq 0$. Since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ is a bounded linear operator the first condition of equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef} follows. Consider the second condition of equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef}. Calculating $\braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{y}\bra{y})}$ for $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ and $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{y}\bra{y})} &= \braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \ket{y_{>t+2}}\bra{y_{>t+2}}\otimes \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}}\bra{y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}}) \otimes \ket{y_{<t}}\bra{y_{<t}}} \nonumber \\
        &= \delta_{x_{>t+2},y_{>t+2}}\delta_{x_{<t},y_{<t}} \braket{\ket{x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}}\bra{x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}}\bra{y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}})} \nonumber \\
        &= \begin{cases}
            \delta_{x_{>t+2},y_{>t+2}}\left(\frac{1}{4} - \delta_{x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}, y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t}}\right) \text{ for } x_{t+2}x_{t+1}x_{t}, y_{t+2}y_{t+1}y_{t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}} \\
            0 \text{ otherwise}
        \end{cases}
    \end{align}
    which implies for $x \neq y$ 
    \begin{equation}
        \braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{y}\bra{y})} \geq 0.
    \end{equation}
    Let $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ with $x \neq y$ calculating $Q_{x,y}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        Q_{x,y} = \braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}(\ket{y}\bra{y})} =  \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}(\ket{y}\bra{y})} \geq 0
    \end{align}
    which validates the second condition of equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef}. Consider the third and final condition given in equation~\eqref{eq:QmatrixDef}. By direct calculation we validate
    \begin{align}
        \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}} Q_{y,x} &= \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}} \braket{\ket{y}\bra{y}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}(\ket{x}\bra{x})} = \braket{\ket{y}\bra{y}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}(P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)})} = 0
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer}. Thus $Q$ is a valid transition-rate matrix for a continuous-time Markov chain over the state space $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$.

    Consider the jump chain associated to $Q$ generated by stochastic matrix $P$ in equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain}. For a finite discrete-time Markov chain it is sufficient to show there exists a unique steady-state with full support to prove that it is irreducible. Define vector
    \begin{equation}
        \pi = \sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}} \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|} \hat{x}.
    \end{equation}
    By construction $\pi$ is normalized since $\sum_{x}\pi_{x} = 1$ with $\pi_{x} \geq 0$ therefore $\pi$ is a valid state of the discrete-time Markov chain. By construction $\pi$ has full support over the state space $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ since for all $x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$, $\pi_{x} > 0$. By direct calculation we find
    \begin{equation}
        P\pi = \sum_{x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}}P_{x, y}\pi_{y} \hat{x} = \sum_{x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}}\left(\delta_{x,y} + \frac{1}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}Q_{x,y}\right)\pi_{y} \hat{x} = \pi + \frac{1}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sum_{x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}}Q_{x,y} = \pi.
    \end{equation}
    Therefore $\pi$ is a steady-state for the jump chain with full support. To show uniqueness let $\pi'$ be an arbitrary steady-state of the jump chain. From equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain} and the definition of steady-state we find
    \begin{equation}
        P\pi' = \pi' + \frac{1}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}Q\pi' = \pi',
    \end{equation}
    implying
    \begin{equation}
        Q\pi' = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Therefore a steady-state $\pi'$ must lie in the kernel of $Q$. Since $Q$ is $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}$ expanded in the basis $\{\ket{x}\bra{x} \; x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\}$ we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \dim\ker{Q} = \dim\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}}.
    \end{equation}
    Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} implies $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}} = P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ implying 
    \begin{equation}
        \dim\ker{Q} = 1.
    \end{equation}
    Since the kernel of $Q$ is one dimensional it must contain only a single steady-state vector given by the $\pi$ we found. Therefore the jump chain associated to $Q$ is irreducible.

    To show that the jump chain is reversible we require $P_{x,y}\pi_{y} = P_{y,x}\pi_{x}$ for steady-state $\pi$. By direct calculation we validate
    \begin{align}
        P_{x,y}\pi_{y} &= \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}P_{x,y} = \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\left(\delta_{x,y} + \frac{Q_{x,y}}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}\right) = \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\left(\delta_{x,y} + \frac{1}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}\braket{\ket{x}\bra{x}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}(\ket{y}\bra{y})}\right) \nonumber \\
        &= \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\left(\delta_{x,y} + \frac{1}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}\braket{\ket{y}\bra{y}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}(\ket{x}\bra{x})}^{*}\right) = \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\left(\delta_{y,x} + \frac{Q_{y,x}^{*}}{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}\right) = \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}P_{y,x} \nonumber \\
        &= P_{y,x}\pi_{x},
    \end{align}
    where the second line follows from $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}$ being Hermitian with respect to the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. Therefore the jump chain is reversible implying the statement of Lemma.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lm:Qcalc}
    Let $Q$ be the transition-rate matrix defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Q} of Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain}. For all $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ and $t \in \{0, 1, 2, \cdots, T-3 \}$, we have
    \begin{equation}
        Q_{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}, x_{>t+2}by_{<t}} \geq 1 /4,
    \end{equation}
    for $a, b \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $a \neq b$ where $\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:localillandlegstrings}.
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
We proceed by direct calculation,
    \begin{align}
        Q_{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}, x_{>t+2}by_{<t}} &= \braket{\ket{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}}\bra{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}(\ket{x_{>t+2}by_{<t}}\bra{x_{>t+2}by_{<t}})} \nonumber \\
        &= \sum_{t'=0}^{T-3}\braket{\ket{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}}\bra{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t'+2,t'+1,t')}(\ket{x_{>t+2}by_{<t}}\bra{x_{>t+2}by_{<t}})}.
    \end{align}
    Since $a \neq b$ we find
    \begin{align}
        Q_{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}, x_{>t+2}by_{<t}} = &\braket{\ket{a}\bra{a}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b}\bra{b})} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})} \delta_{a_{t},b_{t}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})} \delta_{a_{t},b_{t}} \delta_{a_{t+1},b_{t+1}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})}\delta_{a_{t+2}, b_{t+2}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})}\delta_{a_{t+2},b_{t+2}}\delta_{a_{t+1},b_{t+1}},
    \end{align}
    which simplifies to become
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:fulllower}
        Q_{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}, x_{>t+2}by_{<t}} = &\frac{1}{4} + \braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})} \delta_{a_{t},b_{t}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})}  \delta_{a_{t+1}a_{t},b_{t+1}b_{t}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})}\delta_{a_{t+2}, b_{t+2}} \nonumber \\
        &+ \braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})}\delta_{a_{t+2}a_{t+1},b_{t+2}b_{t+1}},
    \end{align}
    since $a, b \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $a \neq b$. 

    Consider the term $\braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})} \delta_{a_{t},b_{t}} $. For $a_{t} \neq b_{t}$ this term is zero. For $a_{t} = b_{t}$ we have $a_{t+2}a_{t+1} \neq b_{t+2}b_{t+1}$ since $a \neq b$. For $x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})} &= \frac{1}{4}
    \end{align}
    otherwise 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})} &= 0
    \end{align}
    Thus we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}a_{t+2}a_{t+1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}\bra{x_{t+3}b_{t+2}b_{t+1}})}  \geq 0.
    \end{align}

    Consider the term $\braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})} \delta_{a_{t+1}a_{t},b_{t+1}b_{t}}$. For $a_{t+1}a_{t} \neq b_{t+1}b_{t}$ this term is zero. For $a_{t+1}a_{t} = b_{t+1}b_{t}$ we have $a_{t+2} \neq b_{t+2}$ since $a \neq b$. For $x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})} &= \frac{1}{4}
    \end{align}
    otherwise 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})} &= 0
    \end{align}
    Thus we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}a_{t+2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}}\bra{x_{t+4}x_{t+3}b_{t+2}})} \geq 0
    \end{align}

    Consider the term $\braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})} \delta_{a_{t+2},b_{t+2}}$. For $a_{t+2} \neq b_{t+2}$ this term is zero. For $a_{t+2} = b_{t+2}$ we have $a_{t+1}a_{t} \neq b_{t+1}b_{t}$ since $a \neq b$. For $b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})} &= \frac{1}{4}
    \end{align}
    otherwise 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})} &= 0
    \end{align}
    Thus we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{a_{t+1}a_{t}y_{t-1}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}}\bra{b_{t+1}b_{t}y_{t-1}})} &\geq 0
    \end{align}

    Consider the final term $\braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})} \delta_{a_{t+2}a_{t+1},b_{t+2}b_{t+1}}$. For $a_{t+2}a_{t+1} \neq b_{t+2}b_{t+1}$ this term is zero. For $a_{t+2}a_{t+1} = b_{t+2}b_{t+1}$ have $a_{t} \neq b_{t}$ since $a \neq b$. For $b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})} &= \frac{1}{4}
    \end{align}
    otherwise 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})} &= 0
    \end{align}
    Thus we find
    \begin{align}
        \braket{\ket{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{a_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}(\ket{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}}\bra{b_{t}y_{t-1}y_{t-2}})} &\geq 0
    \end{align}

    Revisiting equation~\eqref{eq:fulllower} we conclude
    \begin{align}
        Q_{x_{>t+2}ay_{<t}, x_{>t+2}by_{<t}} \geq \frac{1}{4}.
    \end{align}
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
Let $G = (\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}, E)$ be the transition graph associated to the jump chain of $Q$ 
    where $Q$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Q} of Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain}. Let $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ and $\gamma_{x,y}$ be the sequence of edges defined according to equations~\eqref{eq:seq1} and~\eqref{eq:seq2}, then $\gamma_{x,y}$ is a path from $x$ to $y$ in $G$.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Assume every $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ is contained in $E$. By construction $\gamma_{x,y}$ is walk from vertex $x$ to vertex $y$ with all cycles removed, therefore it is a path. Thus it suffices to show that for all $x,y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ if $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ then $e \in E$. Since $x,y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ there exists at least one index $s \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ such that $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$, and similarly for $y$, there exists at least one index $f \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ such that $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$. Therefore, for $\gamma_{x,y}$ there exists two cases, either $f - s \geq 0$ or $f-s < 0$.

    Consider the case of $f-s \geq 0$. $\gamma_{x,y}$ is defined according to the sequence of vertices of equation~\eqref{eq:seq1}. Let $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$, we find three cases. Either $e$ is defined from the Phase 1 portion of the sequence, the Phase 2 portion of the sequence, or the Phase 3 portion of the sequence. Consider the first of these three cases. Either $e = (x, x_{>s+1}10x_{<s})$ or there exists some $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, s\}$ such that $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t}10x_{<t-1})$. If $e = (x, x_{>s+1}10x_{<s})$, since $\gamma_{x,y}$ only contains edges between distinct vertices we have $x \neq x_{>s+1}10x_{<s}$ implying $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \neq x_{s+2}10$. Since $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $x_{s+2}10 \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} implying $Q_{e} \geq 1 /4$. Thus we have $P_{e} > 0$ from equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain} implying $e \in E$. Similarly, if $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t}10x_{<t-1})$ for some $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots s \}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} as well, giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 / 4$ and thus $P_{e} > 0$ implying $e \in E$. Consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined through the Phase 2 sequence of vertices. Thus there exists some index $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots T-3\}$ such that $e = (x_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$. Similarly, we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 / 4$ implying $P_{e} > 0$ and thus $e \in E$. Finally, consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ such that $e$ is defined through the Phase 3 sequence of vertices given in equation~\eqref{eq:seq1}. We have two cases, either there exists a $t \in \{f, f+1, \cdots, T-2\}$ such that $e=(y_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, y_{>t}10y_{<t-1})$ or $e = (y_{>f+1}10y_{<f}, y)$. Since the edges only exist in $\gamma_{x,y}$ if the vertices are distinct, and $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f}, y_{f+2}10 \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} in both cases giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 /4$ and thus $P_{e} > 0$ implying $e \in E$. Therefore in the case of $f- s \geq 0$, for all $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$, $e \in E$.

    Consider the case of $f-s < 0$. $\gamma_{x,y}$ is defined according to the sequence of vertices of equation~\eqref{eq:seq2}. Let $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$, we find three cases again. Either $e$ is defined from the Phase 1 portion of the sequence, the Phase 2 portion of the sequence, or the Phase 3 portion of the sequence. Consider the first of these three cases. Either $e = (x, x_{>s+2}10x_{<s+1})$ or there exists some $t \in \{s, s+1, \cdots, T-3\}$ such that $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10x_{<t+1})$. If $e = (x, x_{>s+2}10x_{<s+1})$, since $\gamma_{x,y}$ only contains edges between distinct vertices we have $x \neq x_{>s+2}10x_{<s+1}$ implying $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \neq 10x_{s}$. Since $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $10x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} implying $Q_{e} \geq 1 /4$. Thus we have $P_{e} > 0$ from equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain} implying $e \in E$. Similarly, if $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10x_{<t+1})$ for some $t \in \{s, s+1, \cdots, T-3 \}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} as well, giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 / 4$ and thus $P_{e} > 0$ implying $e \in E$. Consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined through the Phase 2 sequence of vertices. Thus there exists some index $t \in \{1, \cdots T-2\}$ such that $e = (y_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, y_{>t}10x_{<t-1})$. Similarly, we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 / 4$ implying $P_{e} > 0$ and thus $e \in E$. Finally, consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ such that $e$ is defined through the Phase 3 sequence of vertices given in equation~\eqref{eq:seq1}. We have two cases, either there exists a $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, f\}$ such that $e=(y_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, y_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$ or $e = (y_{>f+2}10y_{<f+1}, y)$. Since the edges only exist in $\gamma_{x,y}$ if the vertices are distinct, and $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f}, 10y_{f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we can apply Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc} in both cases giving us $Q_{e} \geq 1 /4$ and thus $P_{e} > 0$ implying $e \in E$. Therefore in the case of $f- s < 0$, for all $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$, $e \in E$.

    In both cases we find for all $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$, we have $e \in E$, we conclude that $\gamma_{x,y}$ is a path from $x$ to $y$ in $G$.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lm:pathlength}
    Let $G = (\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}, E)$ be the transition graph associated to the jump chain of $Q$ 
    where $Q$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Q} of Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain}. Let $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ and $\gamma_{x,y}$ be the path defined according to equations~\eqref{eq:seq1} or~\eqref{eq:seq2}, then 
    \begin{equation}
        |\gamma_{x,y}| \leq 3T.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Each $\gamma_{x,y}$ is defined via the associated walk given by the sequence of vertices in either equation~\eqref{eq:seq1} or equation~\eqref{eq:seq2}. In both cases since $s, f \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ there are at most $3(T-3)$ vertices in each sequence implying the walk defining $\gamma_{x,y}$ has at most $3(T-3) - 1$ edges. Since removing cycles and self-edges only reduces the number of edges in the resulting sequence we find
    \begin{equation}
        |\gamma_{x,y}| \leq 3T.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lm:edgeoverload}
    Let $G = (\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}, E)$ be the transition graph associated to the jump chain of $Q$ 
                                              
    where $Q$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Q} of Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain}. Let $e \in E$ and $\gamma_{x,y}$ be a path from $x$ to $y$ in $G$ defined according to equations~\eqref{eq:seq1} or~\eqref{eq:seq2}, then
    \begin{equation}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| \leq 8|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Fix $e \in E$. Either there exists $(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2}$ such that $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ or for all $(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2}, e \notin \gamma_{x,y}$. Consider the former case of $(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2}$ such that $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$. We have three cases, either $e$ is defined according to the Phase 1 sequence of vertices, the Phase 2 sequence of vertices, or the Phase 3 sequence of vertices described in either equation~\eqref{eq:seq1} or equation~\eqref{eq:seq2}. Without loss of generality assume $\gamma_{x,y}$ is generated according to the sequence of vertices described in equation~\eqref{eq:seq1}.

    Consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined according to the sequence given in Phase 1. Either $e = (x, x_{>s+1}10x_{<s})$ or there exists an index $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, s\}$ such that $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t}10x_{<t-1})$. If $e = (x, x_{>s+1}10x_{<s})$ we find 
    \begin{equation}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| \leq |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{equation}
    If $e = (x_{>t+1}10x_{<t}, x_{>t}10x_{<t-1})$ for some $t \in \{1, 2, \cdots, s\}$ we find 
    \begin{equation}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| \leq 2|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{equation}
    Thus for all $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ defined according to the sequence given in Phase 1 we have 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:phase1}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| \leq 2 |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{equation}

    Consider the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined according to the sequence given in Phase 2. There exists an index $t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}$ such that $e = (x_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$. There exists three cases 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $s \leq t$ and $t \leq f$,
        \item $s \leq t$ and $f \leq t$,
        \item $t \leq s$ and $t \leq f$.
    \end{enumerate}

    Consider the first of these three cases. Since we are promised $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have $x_{\leq s+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(s+3)}$ and $y_{\geq f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-f)}$ which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:case1constraints}
        x_{\leq t+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(t+3)} \text{ and } y_{\geq t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-t)}.
    \end{equation}
    Since our edge $e = (x_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$ fixes $x_{>t+2}$ and $y_{<t}$ with only constraints on $x_{\leq t+2}$ and $y_{\geq t}$ being equation~\eqref{eq:case1constraints} we find
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:case1e1}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(t+3)}| |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-t)}| = (2^{t+3} - (t+3))(2^{T-t} - (T-t)) \leq 2^{t+3}(2^{T-t} - (T-t)) \nonumber \\
        &\leq 2^{T + 3} - (T-t)2^{t+3} = 2^{T+3} - f(t).
    \end{align}
    Calculating $\Delta f$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \Delta f = f(t+1) - f(t) = (T-t-1)2^{t+4} - (T-t)2^{t+3} = [T - t - 2 ]2^{t+3} > 0 \text{ for all } t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}.
    \end{align}
    Thus the minimum of $f(t)$ occurs at $t=0$ implying
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:case1e2}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq 8 (2^{T} - T) = 8 |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}

    Consider the case of $s \leq t$ and $f \leq t$. Since we are promised $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$  we have $x_{\leq s+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(s+3)}$ and $y_{\leq f+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(f+3)}$ which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:case2constraints}
        x_{\leq t+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(t+3)} \text{ and } y_{\leq t+2} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(t+3)}.
    \end{equation}
    Since our edge $e = (x_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$ fixes $x_{>t+2}$ and $y_{<t}$ with the only constraints on $x_{\leq t+2}$ and $y_{\geq t}$ being equation~\eqref{eq:case2constraints} and $y_{\geq t} \in \{0, 1\}^{T-t}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(t+3)}|2^{T-t} = (2^{t+3} - (t+3))2^{T-t} = 2^{T+3} - (t+3)2^{T-t} = 2^{T+3} - f(t).
    \end{align}
    Calculating $\Delta f$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \Delta f = f(t+1) - f(t) = (t+4)2^{T-t-1} - (t+3)2^{T-t} = \left(-\frac{t}{2} - 1\right)2^{T-t} < 0  \text{ for all } t \in \{0, 1, \cdots, T-3\}.
    \end{align}
    Thus the minimum of $f(t)$ occurs at $t=T-3$ implying
    \begin{align}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq 8 (2^{T} - T) = 8 |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}

    Consider the final case of $t \leq s$ and $t \leq f$. Since we are promised $x_{s+2}x_{s+1}x_{s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ and $y_{f+2}y_{f+1}y_{f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}$ we have $x_{\geq s} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-s)}$ and $y_{\geq f} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-f)}$ which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:case3constraints}
        x_{\geq t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-t)} \text{ and } y_{\geq t} \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-t)}.
    \end{equation}
    Since our edge $e = (x_{>t+1}10y_{<t}, x_{>t+2}10y_{<t+1})$ fixes $x_{>t+2}$ and $y_{<t}$ with the only constraints on $x_{\leq t+2}$ and $y_{\geq t}$ being equation~\eqref{eq:case3constraints} and $x_{\leq t+2} \in \{0, 1\}^{t+3}$, we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T-t)}|2^{t+3} = (2^{T-t} - (T-t))2^{t+3} \leq 8|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|,
    \end{align}
    where the last inequality follows from applying equations~\eqref{eq:case1e1} and~\eqref{eq:case1e2}.

    Thus, for the case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined according to the sequence given in Phase 2, we conclude from all three cases that
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:phase2}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq  8|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}

    Consider the final case of $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ being defined according to the sequence of vertices of Phase 3. Either $e = (y_{>f+2}10y_{<f}, y)$ or there exists a $t \in \{f, f+1, \cdots T-3\}$ such that $e = (y_{>t+1}10y_{y<t}, y_{>t}10y_{<y-1})$. If $e = (y_{>f+2}10y_{<f}, y)$ we find
    \begin{align}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq |\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}
    If $e = (y_{>t+1}10y_{y<t}, y_{>t}10y_{<y-1})$ for some $t \in \{f, f+1, \cdots, T-3\}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq 2|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}
    Therefore, for all $e \in \gamma_{x,y}$ defined according to the sequence given in Phase 3 we have 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:phase3}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq 2|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|.
    \end{align}

    From equations~\eqref{eq:phase1}, \eqref{eq:phase2}, and~\eqref{eq:phase3} we conclude that for $e \in E$,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:phase3}
        |\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times 2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}| &\leq 8|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|
    \end{align}
    as stated.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lm:DunaryD}
    Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define subspace  $\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:subspacedefs}, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}\right) \geq 1 / 96T^{2}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
Since $Q$ is $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}$ expanded in the basis $\{\ket{x}\bra{x} \; | \; x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)} \}$ we immediately have
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:relationtoQ}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}}\right) = \mathrm{gap}\left(Q\right).
    \end{equation}
    From equation~\eqref{eq:jumpchain} we have $Q = \left\lVertQ\right\rVert(P - \mathbb{I})$ where $P$ is the stochastic matrix generating the jump chain associated to $Q$. From Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain} and $P \succeq 0$ we have,
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(Q\right) = \left\lVertQ\right\rVert\left(1 - \lambda_{1}(P)\right),
    \end{equation}
    where $\lambda_{i}(P)$ denotes the $i$\textsuperscript{th} eigenvalue of $P$ ordered such that $\lambda_{i}(P) \geq \lambda_{i+1}(P)$ with $i \in \{0, 1, \cdots\}$.

    Let $G = (S_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}, E)$ be the transition graph associated to the jump chain of $Q$. For all edges $e = (x,y) \in E$ define the weight of an edge $w(e) = w(x,y) = \pi_{x} P_{x,y}$ where $\pi$ is the steady-state of the jump chain found in equation~\eqref{eq:steadystate} of Lemma~\ref{lm:blockismarkovchain}. Let $\Gamma$ the set of canonical paths over $G$ where $\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma$ is the path from $x$ to $y$ defined according to the sequence of vertices given in equation~\eqref{eq:seq1} or equation~\eqref{eq:seq2}. Define the congestion associated to $\Gamma$ as 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:congestion}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) = \sup_{e \in E} \left(\frac{1}{w(e)} \sum_{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma} \pi_{x}\pi_{y} |\gamma_{x,y}|\mathbf{1}[e \in \gamma_{x,y}]\right).
    \end{equation}
    where $\mathbf{1}$ denotes the indicator function. From Theorem 5 of \cite{sinclair1992Improved} we can upper-bound 
    \begin{equation}
        \lambda_{1}(P) \leq 1 - \frac{1}{\bar{\rho}(\Gamma)}
    \end{equation}
    implying 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(Q\right) \geq \frac{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}{\bar{\rho}(\Gamma)}.
    \end{equation}

    We proceed to lower-bound $\mathrm{gap}\left(Q\right)$ by upper-bounding the congestion. From our definition of $w$ we find
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:wlowerbnd}
        w(e) = w(x,y) = \pi_{x}P_{x,y} = \frac{P_{x,y}}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|} = \frac{Q_{x,y}}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|\left\lVertQ\right\rVert} \text{ for } x \neq y.
    \end{equation}


    Calculating the congestion defined in equation~\eqref{eq:congestion} we find
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:congestion1}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) = \frac{1}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|^{2}}\sup_{e \in E} \left(\frac{1}{w(e)} \sum_{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma}  |\gamma_{x,y}|\mathbf{1}[e \in \gamma_{x,y}]\right).
    \end{equation} 
    Since the term inside the supremum is only non-zero for the edges contained in a path inside $\Gamma$, we have the additional constraints that $e = (x,y)$ where $x \neq y$ along with $e$ being defined according to the sequence of vertices given in equation~\eqref{eq:seq1} or equation~\eqref{eq:seq2}. Thus equation~\eqref{eq:congestion1} becomes
    \begin{equation}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) \leq \frac{\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sup_{e \in E} \left(\frac{1}{Q_{e}}\sum_{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma}  |\gamma_{x,y}|\mathbf{1}[e \in \gamma_{x,y}]\right) \leq \frac{4\left\lVertQ\right\rVert}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sup_{e \in E} \left(\sum_{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma}  |\gamma_{x,y}|\mathbf{1}[e \in \gamma_{x,y}]\right) 
    \end{equation} 
    where the first inequality follows from equation~\eqref{eq:wlowerbnd} and the second follows from applying Lemma~\ref{lm:Qcalc}. Applying Lemma~\ref{lm:pathlength} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) \leq \frac{12\left\lVertQ\right\rVert T}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sup_{e \in E} \left( \sum_{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma}  \mathbf{1}[e \in \gamma_{x,y}]\right) = \frac{12\left\lVertQ\right\rVert T}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sup_{e \in E}|\{\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}|.
    \end{equation} 
    Since for all $x, y \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}$ there exists a unique $\gamma_{x,y} \in \Gamma$ we can simplify the above equation as
    \begin{equation}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) \leq  \frac{12\left\lVertQ\right\rVert T}{|\mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}|}\sup_{e \in E}|\{(x,y) \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)\times2} \; | \; e \in \gamma_{x,y}\}|.
    \end{equation} 
    Applying Lemma~\ref{lm:edgeoverload} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \bar{\rho}(\Gamma) \leq  96\left\lVertQ\right\rVert T,
    \end{equation}
    which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:gapQ}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(Q\right) \geq \frac{1}{96\left\lVertQ\right\rVert T}.
    \end{equation}

    Upper-bounding $\left\lVertQ\right\rVert$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        \left\lVertQ\right\rVert = \left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq \left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq  \sum_{t=0}^{T-3}\left\lVert\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(t+2,t+1,t)}\right\rVert_{\infty} \leq T.
    \end{align}
    Combining the above equation along with equations~\eqref{eq:relationtoQ} and~\eqref{eq:gapQ} we conclude with
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}\right) \geq \frac{1}{96T^{2}}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proof-58 -->
<!-- proposition--4: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}, then 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) = 1 / 96T^{3}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition--4 -->
<!-- proof-59: body_md -->
Since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ acts only on the clock register $C$  we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) =  \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{C})}\right).
    \end{equation}
    From Lemma~\ref{lm:Dublockdiag} and Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} we find
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) =  \inf\left\{\mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{O}}\right), \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}|_{\mathbb{D}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}}\right)\right\}.
    \end{equation}
    Applying Lemmas~\ref{lm:DunaryO} and~\ref{lm:DunaryD} we conclude with
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{gap}\left(\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}\right) \geq  \inf\left\{\frac{1}{4T^{3}}, \frac{1}{96T^{2}}\right\} = \frac{1}{96T^{3}}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proof-59 -->
<!-- lemma--7: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}$ be the Lindbladian dissipator defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dunary} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} and define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:globalillandlegsubspaces} and
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} \; \big| \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)} \times [\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}]^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\},
    \end{equation}
    then the overlap between $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}$ and $\mathsf{M}$ is given by 
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}, A \in \mathsf{M} \\ \braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = \braket{A, A} = 1}} |\braket{A_{0}, A}|^{2} \leq \frac{1}{2^{T} -T}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma--7 -->
<!-- proof-60: body_md -->
From Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} we have for all $A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}$  
    \begin{equation}
        A_{0} = B + C_{MA}\otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}
    \end{equation}
    for $B \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA}) \otimes \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)})$ and $C = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA})$. Let $\braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = 1$, we find
    \begin{align}
        1 = \braket{B, B} + \braket{C, C}\left(2^{T} - T\right)
    \end{align}
    which implies
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:Cupperbound}
        \begin{cases}
            \braket{B, B} \leq 1 \\
            \braket{C, C} \leq 1 / (2^{T} - T)
        \end{cases}.
    \end{equation}
    Let $A \in \mathsf{M}$ and $\braket{A, A} = 1$, we have 
    \begin{equation}
        A = v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp},
    \end{equation}
    and 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:v3upper}
        1 = |v_{1}|^{2} + |v_{2}|^{2} + |v_{3}|^{2}.
    \end{equation}
    Directly calculating $\braket{A, A_{0}}$ we find 
    \begin{align}
        \braket{A, A_{0}} &=  v_{1}^{*}\bra{\perp}B\ket{h} + v_{1}^{*}\bra{\perp}C \otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\ket{h} + v_{2}^{*}\bra{h}B\ket{\perp} \nonumber \\
        &\quad + v_{2}^{*}\bra{h}C\otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\ket{\perp} + v_{3}^{*}\bra{\perp}B\ket{\perp} + v_{3}^{*}\bra{\perp}C \otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\ket{\perp} \nonumber \\
        &= v_{3}^{*}\bra{\perp}C \otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\ket{\perp} = \sum_{a}\sum_{x \in \mathrm{S}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}}v_{3}^{*}c_{a,x}\bra{\perp}C\otimes P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\ket{a}_{MA}\otimes \ket{x}_{C} \nonumber \\
        &= v_{3}^{*}\operatorname{Tr}\left(C_{MA} \otimes \mathbb{I}_{C}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}\right) = v_{3}^{*}\operatorname{Tr}\left(C Tr_{C}\left(\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}\right)\right) = v_{3}^{*}\operatorname{Tr}\left(C \rho\right)
    \end{align}
    where we have defined the quantum state $\rho = \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}\right)$.
    Thus we find 
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{A, A_{0}}|^{2} = |v_{3}|^{2} |\braket{C, \rho}|^{2} \leq |\braket{C, \rho}|^{2} \leq  \braket{C, C} \braket{\rho, \rho} \leq  \braket{C, C} \leq 1 / (2^{T} - T)
    \end{align}
    where the first inequality follows from equation~\eqref{eq:v3upper}, the second from Cauchy-Schwarz, the third from $\braket{\rho, \rho}$ being equal to the purity of the quantum state $\rho$ and thus upper-bounded by $1$, and the final from equation~\eqref{eq:Cupperbound}. Therefore we conclude,
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}}, A \in \mathsf{M} \\ \braket{A_{0}, A_{0}} = \braket{A, A} = 1}} |\braket{A_{0}, A}|^{2} \leq \frac{1}{2^{T} - T}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end proof-60 -->
<!-- lemma--8: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal{L}_{1}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ be Hermitian Lindbladians acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}) = \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} \oplus (\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}})^{\perp}$, define subspace $\mathcal{H}_{1} = \mathrm{span}(\{\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H} \; | \; \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} \})$ which denotes the span of all pure steady states of $\mathcal{L}_{1}$. If $\mathcal{H}_{1} \neq \emptyset$ and $(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) \geq 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}$, then for all $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq \inf_{\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}}|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}|_{\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}|- \frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}},
    \end{equation}
    where 
    \begin{equation}
        \cos^{2}\theta = \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}, A \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A , A } = 1}} |\braket{A_{0},A}|^{2} 
    \end{equation}
    denotes the overlap between $\ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}$ and
    \begin{equation}
        \mathsf{M} = \left\{ v_{1}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + v_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + v_{3}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{1})^{\perp} \; | \; (\ket{h}, \ket{\perp}, v) \in \mathcal{H}_{1} \times \mathcal{H}_{1}^{\perp} \times \mathbb{C}^{3} \right\}.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end lemma--8 -->
<!-- proof-61: body_md -->
Assume $\mathcal{H}_{1} \neq \emptyset$. We can partition $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_{1} \oplus \mathcal{H}_{1}^{\perp}$ implying for all $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$ there exists a $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}$ and $\ket{\perp} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}^{\perp}$ such that $\ket{\psi} = \alpha_{1}\ket{h} + \alpha_{2}\ket{\perp}$ for $\alpha_{1}^{2} + \alpha_{2}^{2} = 1$. 
    Without loss of generality we take $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2} \geq 0$ implying $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2} \in [0,1]$. Calculating $\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}$, we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} = \alpha_{1}^{2}\ket{h}\bra{h} + \alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + \alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + \alpha_{2}^{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp} = \alpha_{1}^{2} \ket{h}\bra{h} + \tilde{A}_{\perp},
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined $A_{\perp} = \alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\ket{h}\bra{\perp} + \alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{h} + \alpha_{2}^{2}\ket{\perp}\bra{\perp}$. Similarly, we can calculate $\braket{\tilde{A}_{\perp},\tilde{A}_{\perp}}$ finding,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:normofperp}
        \braket{\tilde{A}_{\perp},\tilde{A}_{\perp}} = 2\alpha_{1}^{2}\alpha_{2}^{2} + \alpha_{2}^{4} = (2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})\alpha_{2}^{2}.
    \end{equation}
    
    Assume $\braket{\tilde{A}_{\perp},\tilde{A}_{\perp}}=0$, we find from the above equation and $\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2} \in [0,1]$ that $\alpha_{2}=0$. Since $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{1}$ we have $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{1}}$ which implies the statement of the lemma. Thus we assume $\alpha_{2} \neq 0$ implying we can normalize $\tilde{A}_{\perp}$ allowing us to write
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} = \alpha_{1}^{2} \ket{h}\bra{h} + \sqrt{\braket{\tilde{A}_{\perp}, \tilde{A}_{\perp}}}A_{\perp} = \alpha_{1}^{2}\ket{h}\bra{h} + \alpha_{2}\sqrt{2 - \alpha_{2}^{2}}A_{\perp}
    \end{equation}
    where we have defined $A_{\perp} = \tilde{A}_{\perp} / \sqrt{\braket{\tilde{A}_{\perp}, \tilde{A}_{\perp}}}$.


    Calculating the decay of $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}$ under $\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2}$, we find, 
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:decay}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| &= - \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{1}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} - \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})} \\
                                                                                                                &= - \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})\braket{A_{\perp}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{1}(A_{\perp})} - \braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}
    \end{align}
    where the first equality follows from Lemma~\ref{lm:repartL}. Defining $g = -\braket{A_{\perp}, \mathrm{Re}\mathcal{L}_{1}(A_{\perp})}$ and $\mathrm{D} = - \braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:decay1}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| = &\alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}\alpha_{1}^{4} -2\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})}\alpha_{1}^{2}\alpha_{2}\sqrt{2-\alpha_{2}^{2}} \nonumber \\
