                                                                                                                &- \braket{A_{\perp}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})}\alpha_{2}^{2}(2-\alpha_{2}^{2}).
    \end{align}
    Since $\mathcal{L}_{2}$ is Hermitian, $\braket{A_{\perp}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})} = \braket{A_{\perp}, \mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})} \leq 0$. Thus, we can drop the last term in equation~\eqref{eq:decay1} finding
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:decay2}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| &\geq \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}\alpha_{1}^{4} -2\operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})}\alpha_{1}^{2}\alpha_{2}\sqrt{2-\alpha_{2}^{2}} \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                &\geq \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}\alpha_{1}^{4} -2|\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathcal{L}_{2}(A_{\perp})}|\alpha_{1}^{2}\alpha_{2}\sqrt{2-\alpha_{2}^{2}} \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                    &\geq \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}\alpha_{1}^{4} - 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\alpha_{1}^{2}\alpha_{2}\sqrt{2-\alpha_{2}^{2}},
    \end{align}
    where the last inequality follows from $\braket{A_{\perp}, A_{\perp}} = \braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \ket{h}\bra{h}} = 1$ and applying our definition of $\left\lVert\bullet\right\rVert_{\infty}$. Rewriting the lower-bound with respect to $\alpha_{2}$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:decay3}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| &\geq \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}(1-\alpha_{2}^{2})^{2} - 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}(1 - \alpha_{2}^{2})\alpha_{2}\sqrt{2-\alpha_{2}^{2}} \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                        &\geq \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g + \mathrm{D}(1-2\alpha_{2}^{2} + \alpha_{2}^{4}) - 2\sqrt{2}\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}(1 - \alpha_{2}^{2})\alpha_{2} \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                        &\geq \mathrm{D} + \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g - 2\mathrm{D}\alpha_{2}^{2} - 2\sqrt{2}\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\alpha_{2} \nonumber \\
                                                                                                                          &\geq \mathrm{D} + \alpha_{2}^{2}(2 - \alpha_{2}^{2})g - 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\alpha_{2}^{2} - 2\sqrt{2}\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\alpha_{2}
    \end{align}
    where the third inequality follows from $\mathrm{D} = -\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{h}\bra{h})} \geq 0$ which follows from Lemma~\ref{lm:repartL} and the fourth follows from $\mathrm{D} = -\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{h}\bra{h})} = |\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \mathcal{L}_{2}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}| \leq \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}$.

    To calculate $g$, note $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}) = \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}} \oplus \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}^{\perp}$, thus we can expand
    \begin{equation}
        A_{\perp} =  \beta_{1}A_{0} + \beta_{2}A_{g},
    \end{equation}
    where $A_{0} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}$, $A_{g} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}^{\perp}$, and $\braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A_{g}, A_{g}} = 1$.
    Since $\braket{A_{\perp}, A_{\perp}}=1$ we find $|\beta_{1}|^{2} + |\beta_{2}|^{2} = 1$. Plugging this into our definition for $g$ we find,
    \begin{equation}
        g = - \braket{A_{\perp}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\mathcal{L}_{1}(A_{\perp})} = - |\beta_{2}|^{2}\braket{A_{g}, \mathcal{L}_{1}(A_{g})} \geq  (1 - |\beta_{1}|^{2})\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) \geq \left(1 - |\braket{A_{0}, A_{\perp}}|^{2}\right)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right).
    \end{equation}
    Note, from definition we have $A_{\perp} \in \mathsf{M}$ thus we can further lower-bound $g$ as 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:g}
        g \geq \left(1 - \sup_{\substack{A_{0} \in \ker{\mathcal{L}_{1}}, A_{\perp} \in \mathsf{M}\\ \braket{A_{0},A_{0}} = \braket{A_{\perp}, A_{\perp}} = 1}}|\braket{A_{0}, A_{\perp}}|^{2} \right)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) = \left(1 - \cos^{2}\theta \right) \mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) \geq 0.
    \end{equation}
    Therefore applying equation~\eqref{eq:g} to equation~\eqref{eq:decay3} we find 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq  \mathrm{D} - 2\sqrt{2}\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\alpha_{2} + \left[(1 - \cos^{2}\theta) \mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty} \right] \alpha_{2}^{2} = f(\alpha_{2}).
    \end{equation}

    Assume $(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) > 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert$, calculating
    \begin{equation}
        0 = \frac{df}{d\alpha_{2}}\bigg|_{\alpha_{2} = \alpha} = -2\sqrt{2}\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty} + 2\left[(1 - \cos^{2}\theta) \mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\right]\alpha,
    \end{equation}
    which implies $\alpha = \sqrt{2} \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert / \left[(1 - \cos^{2}\theta) \mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}\right]$. Since 
    \begin{equation}
        \frac{d^{2}f}{d\alpha_{2}^{2}}\bigg|_{\alpha_{2} = \alpha} > 0,
    \end{equation}
    $f(\alpha)$ is a global minimum therefore we find 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}, \mathrm{Re}(\mathcal{L}_{1} + \mathcal{L}_{2})(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})}| \geq  f(\alpha) \geq \mathrm{D} - \frac{2\left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}^{2}}{(1 - \cos^{2}\theta)\mathrm{gap}\left(\mathcal{L}_{1}\right) - 2 \left\lVert\mathcal{L}_{2}\right\rVert_{\infty}},
    \end{equation}
    and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:psdecayproj} follows.
<!-- end proof-61 -->
<!-- lemma--9: body_md -->
Let $(V, b,a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:DQCSAT} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}. Let $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ be a pure history state associated to $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi} = \ket{\psi}_{M}\otimes\ket{0}_{A} \in \mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{A}$, then the decay of $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}$  is given by  
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big) \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
<!-- end lemma--9 -->
<!-- proof-62: body_md -->
Consider a pure history state associated $V$ given by $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$. From Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis} we can calculate the action of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ on $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ finding,
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) &= \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) \nonumber \\
                                                                    &= \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}),
    \end{align}
    where the last equality follows from applying Proposition~\ref{prop:propdisker}. Calculating $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) &= \sum_{i=1}^{k}\left((\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{0}\bra{0}_{C})\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}} (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}) - \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}, \ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}\right\}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                      &= \sum_{i=1}^{k}\left(\frac{1}{T}\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\otimes\ket{0}_{C}\bra{0}_{C} - \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}, \ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}\right\}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                      &= -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\left(\ket{\psi}_{M}\otimes(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{0}_{C}\bra{\eta_{\phi}} + \ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes\bra{0}_{A}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}) \otimes \bra{0}_{C}\right) = 0.
    \end{align}
    Calculating $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) = &(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}\otimes\ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C})\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}) \nonumber \\
                                                        &- \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{T-1}\bra{T-1}_{C}, \ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}\right\},
    \end{align}
    which becomes,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:dout}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) = \frac{1}{T}&(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V(\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}_{MA})V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})\otimes\ket{T-1}_{C}\bra{T-1}_{C} \nonumber \\
                                                                   &- \frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi}_{MA} \otimes \ket{T-1}_{C}\bra{\eta_{\phi}} \nonumber \\
                                                                   &- \frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}}\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\phi}_{MA}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}) \otimes \bra{T-1}_{C}.
    \end{align}
    Thus we find $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})$ where $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})$ is given by equation~\eqref{eq:dout}.

    Calculating the decay of $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}$ gives us,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}|.
    \end{equation}
    Applying equation~\eqref{eq:dout}, and our definition of $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ found in equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, we find
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| =  \Big| \frac{1}{T}\bra{\phi}V^{*} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi} - \bra{\phi}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi} \Big|,
    \end{equation}
    which simplifies to 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big| \frac{1}{T} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right) -  1\Big| \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{equation}
    Note, the term inside the absolute value is always less than zero since $0 \leq \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right) \leq 1$, thus
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big)\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right),
    \end{equation}
    implying the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:properdecay} holds.
<!-- end proof-62 -->
<!-- lemma--10: body_md -->
Let $(V, b,a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} and $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}$ defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Dloc} of Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT}.  Let $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ be a pure history state associated to $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi} = \ket{\psi}_{M}\otimes\ket{0}_{A} \in \mathcal{H}_{M}\otimes\mathcal{H}_{A}$, then the decay of $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}$  is given by  
    \begin{align}
        |\braket{\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} &\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big) \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{align}
<!-- end lemma--10 -->
<!-- proof-63: body_md -->
Consider a pure history state associated $V$ given by $\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}$. From Definition~\ref{def:localDQCSAT} we can calculate the action of $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ on $\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}$ finding,
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}} \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) + \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}).
    \end{equation}
    From Proposition~\ref{prop:DuKer} we have $\ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}} = \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA}) \otimes \left(\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)}) \oplus P_{\operatorname{\mathrm{illegal}}}^{(T)}\right)$. In-addition we have have $\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} \subseteq \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA}\otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)})$ where $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ is defined according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hqcirc} of Definition~\ref{def:circsubspace} after having applied the unary map of equation~\eqref{eq:unary} to our clock register $C$. Thus we have $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{unary}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = 0$. A similar argument holds for $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})$ since the mappings given in equations~\eqref{eq:unary} and~\eqref{eq:local} can be reversed on $\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{legal}}}^{(T)})$ giving us $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}(\ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}) = 0$ where $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ denotes the pure history state $\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}$ with the clock register $C$ encoded in binary.

    Calculating $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) &= \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left((\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{0}\bra{0}_{1})\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}} (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{1}) - \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{1}, \ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\right\}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                      &= \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\frac{1}{T}\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{0}\bra{0}_{A}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\otimes\ket{0}\bra{0}^{\otimes T-1}\otimes\ket{1}\bra{1}_{0} - \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}, \ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\right\}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                      &= -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\ket{\psi}_{M}\otimes(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{0}^{\otimes T-1}\otimes \ket{1}_{0} \bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}} + \ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\psi}_{M}\otimes\bra{0}_{A}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}) \otimes \bra{0}^{\otimes T-1} \otimes \bra{1}_{0}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                      & = 0.
    \end{align}
    Calculating $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})$ we find
    \begin{align}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = &(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}\otimes\ket{1}\bra{1}^{\otimes T})\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{1}\bra{1}^{\otimes T}) \nonumber \\
                                                                        &- \frac{1}{2} \left\{\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}} \otimes \ket{1}\bra{1}^{\otimes T}, \ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\right\},
    \end{align}
    which becomes,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:doutloc}
        \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = \frac{1}{T}&(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V(\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}_{MA})V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})\otimes\ket{1}\bra{1}^{\otimes T} \nonumber \\
                                                                   &- \frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi}_{MA} \otimes \ket{1}^{\otimes T}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}} \nonumber \\
                                                                   &- \frac{1}{2\sqrt{T}}\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\phi}_{MA}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}) \otimes \bra{1}^{\otimes T}.
    \end{align}
    Thus we find $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}) = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})$ where $\tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})$ is given by equation~\eqref{eq:doutloc}.

    Calculating the decay of $\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}$ under $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}$ we find,
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}| = |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}| = \Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}} |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \tilde{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}|.
    \end{equation}
    Applying equation~\eqref{eq:doutloc}, and our definition of $\Gamma_{\operatorname{\mathrm{out}}}$ found in equation~\eqref{eq:dissrates} of Definition~\ref{def:QCSATdis}, we find
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, b, a)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}| =  \Big| \frac{1}{T}\bra{\phi}V^{*} (\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi} - \bra{\phi}V^{*}(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}})V\ket{\phi} \Big|,
    \end{equation}
    which simplifies to 
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}| = \Big| \frac{1}{T} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right) -  1\Big| \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right).
    \end{equation}
    Note, the term inside the absolute value is always less than zero since $0 \leq \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right) \leq 1$, thus
    \begin{equation}
        |\braket{\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}, \operatorname{\mathrm{Re}}\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{loc}}}^{(V, a, b)}(\ket{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}}\bra{\tilde{\eta}_{\phi}})}| = \Big(1 - \frac{1}{T} \operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right)\Big)\operatorname{Tr}\left(\ket{0}\bra{0}_{M_{0}}V\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}V^{*}\right),
    \end{equation}
    implying the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:properdecayloc} holds.
<!-- end proof-63 -->
<!-- lemma--11: body_md -->
Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$. Define subspace $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hprop} of Definition~\ref{def:histsubspace} using $V$, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $U^{(V)}$ is given in equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}.
<!-- end lemma--11 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
To show $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$ we require:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For all $\ket{h} \in U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$, $\ket{\eta_{\phi}} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$
        \item For all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, $\ket{h} \in U[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$.
    \end{enumerate}

    Consider the first of these two conditions, for all $\ket{h} \in U[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$ we have $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \operatorname{\mathcal{U}}^{(V)}[\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA}) \otimes \mathrm{span}\left(\{\mathbb{I}_{C}, \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}\}\right)]$ From Proposition~\ref{prop:propdisker} we have $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$ implying $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$, thus we only need to show the second condition in-order to prove the statement.

    Consider the second condition. Let $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ implying $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}^{(V)}}$. From Proposition~\ref{prop:propdisker} we find
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:revstate}
        \sigma = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}(\ket{h}\bra{h}) = \alpha_{1}P_{MA} \otimes \frac{\mathbb{I}_{C}}{T} + \alpha_{2} Q_{MA}\otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} 
    \end{equation}
    for some operators $P, Q \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{MA})$ where $\operatorname{Tr}(P) = \operatorname{Tr}(Q) = 1$ and $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2} \in \mathbb{R}$. Since $\mathcal{U}^{(V)}$ is unitary, $\sigma$ satisfies
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma) = 1$,
        \item $\sigma \succeq 0$,
        \item $\sigma^{2} = \sigma$.
    \end{enumerate}
    From property 3. we find 
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma^{2} - \sigma = \left(\frac{\alpha_{1}^{2}}{T^{2}} P_{MA}^{2} - \frac{\alpha_{1}}{T} P_{MA}\right) \otimes \mathbb{I}_{C} + \frac{\alpha_{1}\alpha_{2}}{T}\{P_{MA}, Q_{MA}\} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} + \alpha_{2}Q_{MA}^{2} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} - \alpha_{2}Q_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C} = 0.
    \end{equation}
    which implies 
    \begin{equation}
        (\mathbb{I}_{MA} \otimes \bra{p^{\perp}}_{C})(\sigma^{2} - \sigma)(\mathbb{I}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p^{\perp}}_{C}) = \frac{\alpha_{1}^{2}}{T^{2}} P^{2} - \frac{\alpha_{1}}{T} P = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Thus $\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P$ is a projector operator. 

    Let $\mathrm{rank}\left(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P\right) > 1$, thus there exists eigenvectors $\ket{v_{1}}$ and $\ket{v_{2}}$ where $\ket{v_{1}} \neq \ket{v_{2}}$, both with eigenvalues of $1$. Calculating the fidelities we find,
    \begin{equation}
        \begin{cases}
            F(\sigma, \ket{v_{1}}_{MA}\otimes\ket{p^{\perp}}_{C}) = \bra{v_{1}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P\right)\ket{v_{1}} = 1, \\
            F(\sigma, \ket{v_{2}}_{MA}\otimes\ket{p^{\perp}}_{C}) = \bra{v_{2}}\left(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P\right)\ket{v_{2}} = 1,
        \end{cases}
    \end{equation}
    which implies $\ket{v_{1}}\bra{v_{1}}_{MA}\otimes\ket{p^{\perp}}\bra{p^{\perp}}_{C} = \sigma =\ket{v_{2}}\bra{v_{2}}_{MA}\otimes\ket{p^{\perp}}\bra{p^{\perp}}_{C}$ which is a contradiction since $\ket{v_{1}} \neq \ket{v_{2}}$. Thus $\mathrm{rank}\left(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P\right) \ngtr 1$. Assume $\mathrm{rank}(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P) = 1$, thus there exists some $\ket{c} \in \mathcal{H}_{MA}$ such that $\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T} P = \ket{c}\bra{c}$. From property 1. we find,
    \begin{equation}
        \operatorname{Tr}(\sigma) = \mathrm{rank}\left(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P\right)T + \alpha_{2}\operatorname{Tr}(Q) = T + \alpha_{2} = 1,
    \end{equation}
    which implies $\alpha_{2} = 1 - T$.  Let $\{\ket{a}\}$ be an orthnormal basis for $\mathcal{H}_{MA}$, we find 
    \begin{align}
        (\bra{a}_{MA}\otimes\bra{p}_{C})\sigma(\ket{a}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}) &= |\braket{a|c}|^{2} + \alpha_{2}\bra{a}Q\ket{a} \leq \sum_{a}\left(|\braket{a|c}|^{2} + \alpha_{2}\bra{a}Q\ket{a}\right) = 1 + \alpha_{2}\operatorname{Tr}(Q) = 1 + \alpha_{2} \nonumber \\
        &\leq 2 - T,
    \end{align}
    which contradicts property 2. for $T > 2$. Thus for $T > 2$, we require $\mathrm{rank}(\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P) = 0$ implying $\frac{\alpha_{1}}{T}P = 0$ forcing equation~\eqref{eq:revstate} to become
    \begin{equation}
        \sigma = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}(\ket{h}\bra{h}) = \alpha_{2} Q_{MA}\otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}.
    \end{equation}
    The above equation along with properties 1., 2., and 3. imply there exists a pure state $\ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}_{MA}$ such that $\alpha_{2}Q = \ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}$ thus we find,
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{h}\bra{h} = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}(\sigma) = \mathcal{U}^{(V)}(\ket{\phi}\bra{\phi}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}\bra{p}_{C}) = \ket{\eta_{\phi}}\bra{\eta_{\phi}}
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{\eta_{\phi}}$ is a pure history state associated to the quantum circuit $V$ with input state $\ket{\phi}$. Thus $\ket{\eta_{\phi}} \in U[\mathcal{H}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}]$, and the statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:onlyhist} follows.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- lemma--12: body_md -->
Let $(V, b, a)$ be an instance of \textsc{Quantum Circuit-SAT} where $V=U_{T-1}U_{T-2}\cdots U_{0}$ with $T > 2$. Define $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ according to equation~\eqref{eq:Hqcirc} of Definition~\ref{def:circsubspace} using $V$, then
    \begin{equation}
        \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]
    \end{equation}
    where $\ket{p} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\ket{t}$ and $U^{(V)}$ is given in equation~\eqref{eq:circrot} of Appendix~\ref{app:A}.
<!-- end lemma--12 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
To show $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} = U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M}\otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$ we require:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item For all $\ket{h} \in U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$, we have $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$
        \item For all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$, we have $\ket{h} \in U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$.
    \end{enumerate}

    Consider the first of these two conditions, for all $\ket{h} \in U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$ we have $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$ through Lemma~\ref{lm:onlyhist}. In-addition,  we have for all $i \in \{0, 1, \cdots, k-1\}$  
    \begin{align}
        (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}) \ket{h} &=  (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}) U^{(V)}(\ket{\phi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C})  = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \delta_{t,0} (\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}) V_{t}(\ket{\phi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A}) \otimes \ket{0}_{C} \nonumber \\
                                                                    &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}) V_{0}(\ket{\phi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A}) \otimes \ket{0}_{C} = 0.
    \end{align}
    Since $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}$ is generated by jump operators $\{\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C}\}_{i = 0}^{k-1}$ we have through Lemma~\ref{lm:restrictdfscond} and the above equation that $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{h}\bra{h}) = 0$. Thus $\ket{h}\bra{h} \in \ker{\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}}$ in-addition to $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$. Therefore $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$.

    Consider the second of the two conditions listed above. Let $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}} \subseteq \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{prop}}}$. Lemma~\ref{lm:onlyhist} implies
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:histt}
        \ket{h} = U^{(V)}(\ket{\phi}_{MA} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}V_{t}\ket{\phi}_{MA}\otimes\ket{t}_{C}.
    \end{equation}
    Calculating $\braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{h}\bra{h})}$ we find,
    \begin{align}
        \label{eq:decayofcirc}
        \braket{\ket{h}\bra{h}, \operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{h}\bra{h})} &= \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\bra{h}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C})\ket{h}\left(\bra{h}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}} \otimes \ket{0}\bra{0}_{C})\ket{h} - 1\right)\right) \nonumber \\
                                                           &=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA}\left(\frac{1}{T}\bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA} - 1\right)\right).
    \end{align}
    
    From the definition of $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$ we have $\operatorname{\mathcal{D}}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{in}}}(\ket{h}\bra{h})=0$, thus
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:decayofcirc1}
        \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\left(\bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA}\left(\frac{1}{T}\bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA} - 1\right)\right) = 0.
    \end{equation}
    Since $\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}}$ is a projection operator, $0 \leq \bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA} \leq 1$ implying each of the terms of left-hand side of equation~\eqref{eq:decayofcirc1} must be zero, thus we find for all $i \in \{0, 1, \cdots, k-1\}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:decayofcirc2}
        \bra{\phi}_{MA}(\ket{1}\bra{1}_{A_{i}})\ket{\phi}_{MA} = 0.
    \end{equation}
    From expanding $\ket{\phi}_{MA}$ in the single qubit subspace of $A_{i}$ as $\ket{\phi}_{MA} = c_{i,0}\ket{0}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{\chi_{0}}_{MA \setminus A_{i}} + c_{i,1}\ket{1}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{\chi_{1}}_{MA \setminus A_{i}}$ and applying equation~\eqref{eq:decayofcirc2} we find for all $i \in \{0, 1, \cdots, k-1\}$ that $c_{i,1}=0$, thus for all $i \in \{0, 1, \cdots, k-1\}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{\phi}_{MA} = \ket{0}_{A_{i}}\otimes\ket{\chi_{0}}_{MA \setminus A_{i}},
    \end{equation}
    which can only be true if there exists some quantum state $\ket{\psi}$ on proof register $M$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{\phi}_{MA} = \ket{\psi}_{M}\otimes\ket{0}_{A}.
    \end{equation}
    Thus from equation~\eqref{eq:histt} we have for all $\ket{h} \in \mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{\mathrm{circ}}}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \ket{h} = U^{(V)}(\ket{\psi}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C})
    \end{equation}
    implying $\ket{h} \in U^{(V)}[\mathcal{H}_{M} \otimes \ket{0}_{A} \otimes \ket{p}_{C}]$. The statement of Lemma~\ref{lm:onlycirc} follows.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- definition--1: body_md -->
Let $H$ be a $2k$-local Hamiltonian acting on $2n$ qubits partitioned into $n$ qubit registers $A$ and $B$ with $H$ given by $\{H_{i}\}_{i=1}^{r=\operatorname{poly}(n)}$ where $\mathbb{I} \succeq H_{i} \succeq 0$ and  if $H_{i}$ acts non-trivially on $k'$ qubits in register $A$ then it also acts non-trivially on $k'$ qubits in register $B$, decide
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ such that $(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \leq a$,
        \item \emph{(reject-case)} For all pure quantum states $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ and $\ket{\phi} \in \mathcal{H}_{B}$, $(\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\phi}_{B}) H (\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\phi}_{B}) \geq b$
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case, where $b-a \geq 1 /\operatorname{poly}(n)$.
<!-- end definition--1 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
\label{def:localdens}
    Let $\{\rho_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m=\operatorname{poly}(n)}$ be a set of $k$-local density matrices where each $\rho_{i}$ acts on  $C_{i} \subseteq \{0, \cdots, n-1\}$ qubits. Decide, 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item \emph{(accept-case)} There exist an $n$-qubit state $\sigma$ such that for all $i \in [m]$, $D(\rho_{i}, \operatorname{Tr}_{\{0, \cdots, n-1\} \setminus C_{i}}\left[\sigma\right]) = 0$
        \item \emph{(reject-case)}  For all $n$-qubit states $\sigma$ there exists an $i \in [m]$ such that $D(\rho_{i}, \operatorname{Tr}_{\{0, \cdots, n-1\} \setminus C_{i}}\left[\sigma\right]) \geq \beta$,
    \end{itemize}
    promised one of these to be the case, where $\beta \geq 1 / \operatorname{poly}(n)$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- proposition--5: body_md -->
For $k \leq \log(n)$, $\textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} \in \mathrm{QMA}$.
<!-- end proposition--5 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
Consider the $\mathrm{QMA}$ verification protocal described in Algorithm~\ref{alg:QMAver}. Each state $\rho_{i}$ acts on $2k$ qubits with $k \leq \log(n)$, therefore each $\rho_{i}$ is a $\operatorname{poly}(n) \times \operatorname{poly}(n)$ matrix implying line 4 can be computed in $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time classical computation. Since \textsc{Conistency of $k$-Local Density Matrice} $\in \mathrm{QMA}$ line 1 compiles a $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ size quantum circuit. Since $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ time classical computation can be mapped to a $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ size quantum circuit, the whole protocol can be compiled into a $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ size quantum circuit and thus is efficient.\\

    \ul{\textbf{Completeness:}} \\

    Let $(F, a, b, A, B)$ be an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian}, thus there exists a pure quantum state $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:acceptcase}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B})H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) \leq a.
    \end{equation}
    Merlin chooses $\rho_{A_{i}} = \operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi})$. Since $(\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}, \beta)$ is an \emph{(accept-case)} instance of \textsc{Consistency of $k$-Local Density Matrices} we have
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Pr}(Q_{A} = \text{accept}) \geq 2 / 3.
    \end{equation}
    Thus the protocol does not reject on line 3 with a probability greater than $2/3$. From equation~\eqref{eq:acceptcase} we find 
    \begin{align}
        a \geq (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B})H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}_{B}) &= \sum_{i=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}\left(H_{i} \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{A}\otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}}\bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B}\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                             &= \sum_{i=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}\left(H_{i} \operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}_{A})\otimes \operatorname{Tr}_{B \setminus B_{i}}(\ket{\bar{\psi}}\bra{\bar{\psi}}_{B})\right) \nonumber \\
                                                                                                               &= \sum_{i=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}\left(H_{i} \rho_{A_{i}} \otimes \bar{\rho}_{A_{i}}\right) = E.
    \end{align}
    Thus if the protocol does not reject on line 3, it will always accept on line 6. Therefore the protocol accepts with a probability at least $2/3$ as required. \\

    \ul{\textbf{Soundness:}} \\

    Let $(F, a, b, A, B)$ be a \emph{(reject-case)} instance of \textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian}, thus for all $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{A}$ and $\ket{\chi} \in \mathcal{H}_{B}$ we have
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:rejectcase}
        (\bra{\psi}_{A} \otimes \bra{\chi}_{B})H(\ket{\psi}_{A} \otimes \ket{\chi}_{B}) \geq b.
    \end{equation}
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
    Merlin sends the set $\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}$, thus the \textsc{Consistency of $k$-Local Density Matrices} query on line 1 either accepts with
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Pr}(Q_{A} = \text{accept}) \leq 1 / 3.
    \end{equation}
    when the set $\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}$ isn't consistent with some $\sigma \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A})$ or 
    \begin{equation}
        \mathrm{Pr}(Q_{A} = \text{accept}) \geq 2 /3 .
    \end{equation}
    when the set $\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}$ does pass the consistency test. When the set does pass the consistency test, then for all $i \in [m]$ there exists a quantum state $\sigma \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A})$ such that 
    \begin{equation}
        D(\rho_{A_{i}}, \operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\sigma)) \leq \beta = \frac{b - a}{8m}.
    \end{equation}
    By the sub-additivity of trace distance with respect to tensor products we find
    \begin{equation}
        D(\rho_{A_{i}}\otimes \bar{\rho}_{B_{i}}, \operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\sigma) \otimes \operatorname{Tr}_{B \setminus B_{i}}(\bar{\sigma}) ) \leq  D(\rho_{A_{i}}, \operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\sigma)) + D(\bar{\rho}_{B_{i}}, \operatorname{Tr}_{B \setminus B_{i}}(\bar{\sigma})) \leq \frac{b - a}{4m}.
    \end{equation}
    Calculating $E$ in line 4 we find 
    \begin{align}
        E &= \sum_{i=1}^{m}\operatorname{Tr}(H_{i}\rho_{A_{i}}\otimes \bar{\rho}_{A_{i}}) \geq \sum_{i=1}^{m}\left(\operatorname{Tr}(H_{i}\operatorname{Tr}_{A \setminus A_{i}}(\sigma) \otimes \operatorname{Tr}_{B \setminus B_{i}}(\bar{\sigma})) - \frac{b-a}{2m}\right) = \operatorname{Tr}(H\sigma_{A} \otimes \bar{\sigma}_{B}) - \frac{b-a}{2} \nonumber \\
          &\geq  \sum_{i,j}p_{i}p_{j}\operatorname{Tr}(H\ket{\psi_{i}}\bra{\psi_{i}}_{A} \otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}_{j}}\bra{\bar{\psi}_{j}}_{B}) - \frac{b-a}{2}  \geq \min_{i,j}(\bra{\psi_{i}}_{A}\otimes \bra{\bar{\psi_{i}}}_{B})H(\ket{\psi_{i}}_{A}\otimes \ket{\bar{\psi}_{i}}) - \frac{b - a}{2} \nonumber \\
          &\geq  b - \frac{b-a}{2} = \frac{a + b}{2} 
    \end{align} 
    where the first inequality follows from Claim 20 of \cite{chailloux2012complexity} and the last inequality follows from equation~\eqref{eq:rejectcase}. Since we have $b - a \geq 1 /\operatorname{poly}(n)$ we find  
    \begin{equation}
        E \geq a  + \frac{1}{\operatorname{poly}(n)},
    \end{equation}
    therefore in this case, when the set $\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}$ is consistent with some quantum state in $\sigma \in \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{A})$ and $Q_{A} = \text{accept}$, the protocol will always reject on line 8. Since in the first case, when the set $\{\rho_{A_{i}}\}_{i=1}^{m}$ is not consistent, the protocol accepts with a probability at most $1/3$, and in the second case, when the set does pass the consistency test, it will always reject, the protocol will accept with a probability at most $1/3$ as required. Therefore $\textsc{Symmetric* Separable $k$-Local Hamiltonian} \in \mathrm{QMA}$.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
